studios.name: Image Studio
studios.shortDescription: Create images from a text prompt or transform your own pictures. Pick a model, aspect ratio and quality in the prompt bar, click Generate, and your images appear in a gallery above it.
studios.fullDescription: Image Studio has a gallery on top and a prompt bar at the bottom. There is no separate text-to-image / image-to-image switch: the studio works in text-to-image mode until you add a reference image, and then switches to an image-to-image version of the same model when one exists. In the prompt bar you can add reference images, type a prompt, open the Model picker (tabs All, Text to Image, Image to Image, provider icons and a search box), set the aspect ratio, resolution (when the model has it), model-specific parameters, an Effect Type (for models that have effects), and a batch size of 1 to 4. A Draw button opens Draw to Edit, Recipes opens the prompt-recipe hub, and the Library button (or Saved) lets you reuse earlier uploads and generations.
keyFeatures: Prompt bar with Model picker (tabs All, Text to Image, Image to Image; provider filter; Search models...)
Reference images: add them with the reference button, drag files onto the studio, or pick from Library; the number allowed depends on the model
Aspect ratio, resolution (shown only for models that have it), model-specific PARAMS, and Effect Type (models with effects)
Batch size stepper from 1 to 4 images per click (shown as n/4)
Swap Face upload for face-swap models
Draw to Edit modal (Draw button) for sketching on an image and generating from it
Gallery with Download, Delete, copy, publish and fullscreen preview
howToSteps: Open Image Studio from the studio tab bar (tab 'Image Studio') or go to /studio/image.

Click the model button in the prompt bar (it shows the current model name) to open the Model list. Use the tabs All, Text to Image or Image to Image, the provider icons (or All Providers) and the Search models... box, then click a model.
Type what you want in the prompt box: 'Describe the image you want to create'.

Optional, to transform your own picture: click the reference-image button (tooltip 'Reference image' or 'Add up to N images'), click 'Upload new' (or 'Upload files' when several are allowed), choose image files (max 10MB each) and, for multi-image models, click Done. You can also drag image files onto the studio, or choose a saved image with Library. The prompt placeholder changes to 'Describe how to transform this image (optional)'.
Click the aspect-ratio button and choose a ratio. If a quality/resolution button is shown, click it and choose a resolution.

Optional: open PARAMS (if shown) for extra settings of the chosen model, open Effect Type (if shown for an image-to-image model), and use the - and + buttons to set how many images to create (1 to 4).
Click Generate. The button shows 'Generating...' until the images arrive.
Your images appear in the gallery. Click one to open a fullscreen preview; hover it to Download or Delete (confirm prompt), copy the prompt, or publish.
To go on from a result, add it again as a reference image (Upload new or Library) and generate again.
gettingStarted: Open Image Studio (/studio/image).
Type a prompt in the prompt bar.
Check the model, aspect ratio and (if shown) resolution buttons.
Click Generate.
Click an image in the gallery to preview it; hover it and use Download to save it.
tips: Add a reference image to move from text-to-image to image-to-image: the studio switches to the model's image-reference version automatically; if the model cannot take references you see '<model> does not support image references.'
Describe subject, style, lighting and composition in the prompt for more predictable results.
Use batch size 2 to 4 to get several options at once.
The studio remembers your prompt, model, settings and gallery in this browser between visits (stored locally).
Use Library to reuse files you uploaded or generated in other studios.
bestPractices: Choose the model first, then the aspect ratio, because available ratios and resolutions depend on the model.
For image-to-image, wait for the reference thumbnail to appear before clicking Generate.
Use clear reference images under 10MB.
Download the images you want to keep; the gallery is stored in your browser (the last 50 images).

faqs.question: How do I do image-to-image?
faqs.answer: Add a reference image with the reference button, drag a file in, or use Library. There is no separate switch.

faqs.question: How big can reference images be?
faqs.answer: Up to 10MB per image.

faqs.question: What is Recipes?

faqs.answer: Yes, your own MuAPI key. If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

studios.name: Video Studio
studios.shortDescription: Create AI video from a prompt, a still image, start and end frames, references or an existing video. Choose a model, then a video mode, duration, aspect ratio and resolution in the prompt bar and click Generate.
studios.fullDescription: Video Studio has a gallery of your videos on top and a prompt bar at the bottom. In the prompt bar you add reference media (images, videos, audio, depending on the model), type a prompt, open the Model picker (tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video, Video Tools), and then use the controls that the selected model provides: a video-mode button (From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video, Transfer motion), a Speed button (some models), a Settings button (Quality and a Generation service choice under Advanced, plus model options such as Seed or Generate audio), Aspect Ratio, Duration, Resolution, and Effect. Only the controls that apply to the chosen model and mode are shown. A Draw button lets you sketch a reference image. Seedance and Veo have extra video tools in the Model picker (continue a result, remove watermark, create a 4K copy).
keyFeatures: Model picker with tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video, Video Tools, provider icons and Search models...
Video-mode menu per model family: From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video, Transfer motion
Reference uploads for images (10MB each), videos (50MB each) and audio (50MB each) where the model accepts them; drag-and-drop works on the upload buttons and on the whole studio
Per-model Settings: Quality, Generation service (Standard, Pro, Fast and so on) and options such as Seed, Generate audio
Seedance video tools (Continue a Seedance 2.0 result, Remove watermark) and Veo video tools (Continue Veo 3.1, Create a 4K copy) inside the Model picker
Extend button on Seedance 2.0 results in the gallery
Gallery with hover actions (Download, Delete, copy, publish) and fullscreen preview
howToSteps: Open Video Studio from the studio tab bar (tab 'Video Studio') or go to /studio/video.

Click the model button in the prompt bar. In the Model list use the tabs All, Text to Video, Image to Video or Video Tools, the provider icons (or All Providers) and the Search models... box, then click a model.

If a video-mode button appears next to the model button, click it (header 'Video mode') and choose what you want to do: From prompt, Animate image, Start & end frames, Use references, Edit video, Extend video or Transfer motion. Each item has a one-line description.

Add the media the mode needs using the upload buttons in the prompt bar (hover for tooltips such as 'Upload start frame', 'Upload end frame', 'Upload up to N reference images', 'Upload up to N reference videos'). Images must be under 10MB; videos and audio under 50MB. You can also pick saved files with Library.
Type your prompt. The placeholder tells you what to write: for example 'Describe the video you want to create', 'Describe how to edit the video', or 'Describe the motion (optional)'.

Set the options that are shown: Speed (if shown), Settings (Quality, Generation service under Advanced, and model options), Aspect Ratio, Effect, Duration and Resolution. Buttons that do not apply to the model are not shown.
Click Generate. The button shows 'Generating...' and is disabled until the video returns (or while an upload is running).
Your video appears at the top of the gallery. Hover a tile to play it, click to open the fullscreen player; use the hover buttons to Download or Delete it (Delete asks to confirm).
To continue a Seedance 2.0 video, hover its tile and click Extend, then describe how to continue and click Generate.
gettingStarted: Open Video Studio (/studio/video).

tips: Start with 'From prompt' for text-to-video, and 'Animate image' to bring a still to life.
Use 'Start & end frames' to control the first and last picture (upload start frame, then end frame).
Use 'Use references' to guide a video with uploaded images, videos or audio on models that accept them.
If you upload a file the current model cannot use, the studio switches to a version of the same family that can, or tells you '<family> does not support <image/video/audio> references.'
Duration, resolution and aspect ratio choices differ by model; if a choice is greyed out the message 'Unavailable for this version' appears.
Prompt, model and gallery are remembered in this browser.
bestPractices: Choose the model and mode first; the other controls depend on them.
Wait for uploads to finish before clicking Generate.
Describe subject, action, setting and camera in one or two sentences.
Download videos you want to keep; the gallery is stored in your browser.

studios.name: Audio Studio
studios.description: Generate music, speech, voice clones and sound with a model picker that covers Suno, Minimax, ElevenLabs, Gemini TTS, Fish Audio, Lyria and MMAudio models, with a built-in audio player and a generation history.
studios.shortDescription: Pick an audio model, fill in the settings that model asks for, click Generate Track, then play and save the result in the built-in player.
studios.fullDescription: Audio Studio has one settings panel on the left and a player area on the right. The panel is built from the model you choose: the Audio Model dropdown lists many music, speech, voice-cloning and sound models, and the fields below it (prompt, style, toggles, sliders, dropdowns, audio upload boxes) change to match the selected model. An Estimated cost line sits above the Generate Track button. When a track is ready it appears in a player with Play/Pause, a seek bar, volume and a Save button, and the last results are kept in a Generation History strip at the bottom of the page.
keyFeatures: Audio Model dropdown with a short description for every model; the form below it changes with the model
Suno models for songs (Create Music, Remix Music, Extend Music, Add Vocals, Add Instrumental, Generate Mashup, Generate Sounds, Convert to WAV) and Suno Voice Cloning

studios.howToUse: Open Audio Studio, choose a model under Audio Model, fill in the fields that appear for that model (for the default Suno Create Music model: Style is required), check Estimated cost, click Generate Track, then play the result and click Save to download it.
howToSteps: Open the Audio Studio tab (route /studio/audio). The settings panel is on the left and the player area on the right.

Under Audio Model, click the dropdown (it shows Suno Create Music at first) and pick the model you want. Each entry shows a one-line description; the chosen model's description also appears under Description.

Fill in the fields shown for that model. Fields marked as required by the model must be completed or you get the message 'Please complete the required field: <field name>'. For Suno Create Music only Style is required; for Minimax Speech HD / Turbo the Prompt and Voice ID are required; for MiniMax Music 3.0 both Prompt and Lyrics are required.

If the model has an upload box (for example Audio URL, Instrumental Audio, Vocal Audio, Voice Sample URL, Mashup Tracks), click the box labelled 'Upload audio track' or drag an audio file onto it. When the upload finishes the box shows the file name and 'Ready to generate'. Click Clear to remove the file.

Optional: use the toggles, sliders and dropdowns (for example Custom Mode, Instrumental, Vocal Gender, Style Weight, Speed, Emotion) to fine-tune the result. For Suno models, turn Instrumental off if you want your Prompt sung as lyrics.
Look at Estimated cost above the button to see the price estimate (it shows 'calculating…' while it updates, or a dash if no estimate is available).
Click Generate Track. The button changes to 'Generating Audio...' and the right side shows 'Generating Soundtrack'. Wait until the player appears.
Under 'Now Playing', press the round Play button to listen, click the bar to jump to a point, use the speaker button (Mute/Unmute) and the volume slider that appears when you hover it.
Click Save to download the audio (mp3 file named after the track title, or generated_audio.mp3).
To try again, click New Generation: your settings stay in place so you can adjust them. Earlier results are listed under 'Generation History' at the bottom; click a card to play it again.
gettingStarted: Open Audio Studio from the studio tabs (route /studio/audio).
Leave Audio Model on Suno Create Music for your first song.
In Style type a genre such as Jazz, Classical, Electronic, Pop, Rock or Hip-hop (this field is required).
Turn Instrumental off if you want vocals, and type lyrics into Prompt (with Instrumental on, no lyrics are sung); optionally type a Title.
Click Generate Track and wait for the player.
Press Play under 'Now Playing', then click Save to download.
tips: Suno's Prompt field is described as the exact lyrics that will be sung; describe the sound in Style and put lyrics only in Prompt.
Suno Create Music starts with Instrumental switched on; switch it off when you want sung lyrics.
Use Negative Tags (for example 'Heavy Metal, Upbeat Drums') to steer Suno away from styles you do not want.
Watch Estimated cost before clicking Generate Track, especially after changing sliders or toggles.
Click a Generation History card to replay earlier results without regenerating.
For Suno Remix Music and Suno Extend Music the model description says the uploaded audio should not exceed 2 minutes.
bestPractices: Pick the model by task: Suno models for songs, Minimax Speech / ElevenLabs / Gemini / Fish models for spoken voice, MM Audio V2 or Suno Generate Sounds for effects and loops, Lyria for short clips.
Fill in the required fields first; the studio stops with a message if one is empty.
Keep voice or source samples clean and short; the Suno Voice Cloning description asks for a clean 10-second recording.
Use New Generation to iterate: your last settings are kept so you only change what you want to improve.
Name your track in Title (when the model has it) so the downloaded file and history card are easy to recognise.

inputDetails.name: Audio Model
inputDetails.description: Dropdown at the top of the left panel; lists every audio model with a one-line description. The fields below change when you pick another model.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Always, before filling anything else
inputDetails.restrictions: Changing the model resets the form to that model's defaults, keeping values for fields that have the same name

inputDetails.name: Prompt
inputDetails.description: Main text box. Its label and hint come from the model (for example 'Prompt (Lyrics)' for Suno Add Vocals). For Suno music models it is described as the lyrics that will be sung; for speech models it is the text to speak; for MM Audio V2 and Lyria it describes the sound or clip.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Required by most models except Suno Create Music, Remix Music, Mashup, Voice Cloning and Convert to WAV
inputDetails.restrictions: Some models list character limits in their hints (for example Suno Remix/Extend: maximum 3000 characters; Minimax Voice Clone preview text: 2000 characters; Lyria 3: up to 2,000 characters)

inputDetails.name: Style
inputDetails.description: Music style text such as Jazz, Classical, Electronic, Pop, Rock, Hip-hop. Placeholder: 'Jazz, Classical, Electronic, Pop, Rock, Hip-hop, etc.'
inputDetails.whenToUse: Suno Create Music, Remix Music, Extend Music, Add Vocals
inputDetails.restrictions: Required for those models; the studio asks you to complete it before generating

inputDetails.name: Custom Mode
inputDetails.description: Toggle on Suno Create Music, Remix Music and Extend Music. Description: 'Enable custom mode for advanced settings.' Switched on by default.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Suno music models
inputDetails.restrictions: Suno only

inputDetails.name: Instrumental
inputDetails.description: Toggle on Suno Create Music, Remix Music, Extend Music and Generate Mashup. Switched on by default. The model hint says that if it is off the prompt is used as the exact lyrics.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Switch off when you want sung lyrics; leave on for a track without vocals
inputDetails.restrictions: Suno only; MiniMax Music 3.0 has a separate toggle named Instrumental Only

inputDetails.name: Title
inputDetails.description: Track title. Placeholder example: 'Peaceful Piano Meditation'. Also used as the name of the downloaded file and the history card.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Suno music models
inputDetails.restrictions: Required for Suno Add Vocals and Suno Add Instrumental

inputDetails.name: Negative Tags
inputDetails.description: Styles to avoid, for example 'Heavy Metal, Upbeat Drums'.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Suno music models
inputDetails.restrictions: Suno only

inputDetails.name: Persona ID / Persona Model
inputDetails.description: Persona ID is a text field for a persona or cloned voice ID; Persona Model is a dropdown with style_persona and voice_persona. The model hint says to choose voice_persona when the ID is a cloned voice from Suno Voice Cloning, which requires model V5 or V5_5.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Applying a saved persona or a cloned Suno voice to a new song
inputDetails.restrictions: Suno Create Music, Remix Music, Extend Music

inputDetails.name: Vocal Gender
inputDetails.description: Dropdown male or female (default male).
inputDetails.whenToUse: Suno music models
inputDetails.restrictions: Suno only

inputDetails.name: Style Weight, Weirdness Constraint, Audio Weight
inputDetails.description: Sliders from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05 (default 0.65). Hints: how strongly the style is followed, how experimental the result is, and the balance of audio features.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Fine-tuning Suno results
inputDetails.restrictions: Suno only

inputDetails.name: Audio upload boxes
inputDetails.description: Box with the text 'Upload audio track' and the hint 'MP3, WAV, M4A up to 20MB'. Click or drag a file in. Mashup Tracks shows two boxes (Track #1, Track #2).
inputDetails.whenToUse: Models that need a source track: Suno Remix / Extend / Add Vocals / Add Instrumental / Generate Mashup / Voice Cloning and Minimax Voice Clone
inputDetails.restrictions: Code enforces 10 MB for audio files and only audio/mpeg (mp3), audio/wav and audio/webm; see limitations

inputDetails.name: Voice ID / Voice
inputDetails.description: Dropdown of preset voices for Minimax Speech, ElevenLabs TTS Turbo 2.5 (named voices such as 'James — Husky, Engaging and Bold'), Eleven v4 and Fish Audio S2.1 Pro.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Speech models
inputDetails.restrictions: Available voices depend on the model

inputDetails.name: Speed, Volume, Pitch, Emotion
inputDetails.description: Minimax Speech sliders: Speed 0.5 to 2, Volume 0.1 to 10, Pitch -12 to 12; Emotion dropdown: happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised, neutral.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Shaping spoken delivery
inputDetails.restrictions: Minimax Speech HD / Turbo

inputDetails.name: Duration
inputDetails.description: MM Audio V2 slider from 1 to 30 (default 8).
inputDetails.whenToUse: Setting the length of an MM Audio V2 clip
inputDetails.restrictions: MM Audio V2 only

studios.modelCapabilities: The Audio Model dropdown lists the models defined in audioModels (packages/studio/src/models.js). Each model declares its own required fields and settings, and the form is generated from that definition. Suno models default to model version V5; the version dropdown is not shown in the form.
studios.modelExplanations: Suno models make full songs and handle remix, extend, add vocals, add instrumental, mashups, sounds, WAV conversion and voice cloning. Minimax Speech HD / Turbo and ElevenLabs / Eleven v4 / Fish Audio models turn text into speech with a chosen voice. Minimax Voice Clone and Suno Voice Cloning create voices from samples. MiniMax Music 3.0 and Lyria models make music from a prompt (MiniMax Music 3.0 also needs lyrics). MM Audio V2 makes audio from a prompt with a Duration. Read the Description shown under Audio Model for the model you pick.
advancedFeatures: Custom Mode toggle on Suno music models
Persona ID and Persona Model for Suno personas and cloned voices
Style Weight, Weirdness Constraint and Audio Weight sliders
Minimax Speech controls: Speed, Volume, Pitch, Emotion, Sample Rate, Bitrate, Channel, Format, Language Boost

advancedFeatureExplanations.explanation: Type a persona or cloned voice ID into Persona ID and pick style_persona or voice_persona in Persona Model. The model hint says voice_persona is for IDs from Suno Voice Cloning and needs model V5 or V5_5 (V5 is the default).

advancedFeatureExplanations.restrictions: Suno Create Music, Remix Music and Extend Music

outputs: One audio track per generation, played in the built-in player

outputDetails.description: The audio URL returned by the model, shown under 'Now Playing' with the title you gave (or the prompt text, or 'Generated <model name>').
postGenerationActions: Click a Generation History card to replay

limitations: Generation needs your MuAPI key and available balance.
Each model has its own required fields; the studio blocks generation until they are filled.
The studio waits for a result by checking every 2 seconds for up to 900 checks (about 30 minutes) before giving up.
Uploaded audio is limited to 10 MB and to mp3, wav or webm files by the upload contract, even though the upload box hint says 'MP3, WAV, M4A up to 20MB'.
The Suno model-version dropdown is not shown; Suno runs on its default version (V5).
Models whose inputs are lists (ElevenLabs Text to Dialogue V3 'Dialogue Script', Gemini TTS 'Speakers' and 'Dialogue Turns') are displayed as plain text boxes.

limitationDetails.impact: Files over 10 MB are rejected (the alert text still says 20MB); m4a files are refused with 'Invalid file type'.
limitationDetails.workaround: Export the file as mp3 or wav under 10 MB and upload again.

limitationDetails.impact: Clicking Generate Track with an empty required field shows 'Please complete the required field: <field>'.
limitationDetails.workaround: Fill the named field (for Suno Create Music that is Style).

limitationDetails.impact: You cannot choose V3.5 to V5.5 from the form; the default V5 is used.
limitationDetails.workaround: None in the studio form.

limitationDetails.impact: Dialogue Script, Speakers and Dialogue Turns appear as simple text boxes, so the expected structure is not guided.
limitationDetails.workaround: Use the single-prompt speech models (Minimax Speech, ElevenLabs TTS Turbo 2.5, Eleven v4, Fish Audio S2.1 Pro) if you only need plain narration.

troubleshooting: If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
'Please complete the required field' means a required box is empty.
'Audio file exceeds 20MB limit.' or 'Invalid file type' means the upload was refused; use an mp3 or wav under 10 MB.
'Audio generation failed' or an error toast means the request failed; check your balance and try again.
No sung vocals on a Suno track: switch Instrumental off and put lyrics in Prompt.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Generation is blocked or fails immediately
steps: If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
Read the red toast in the top-right corner for the error text.
Click Generate Track again.
Note the field name in the message.
Fill that field (Style for Suno Create Music, Prompt and Voice ID for Minimax Speech, an uploaded audio for remix / extend / voice-clone models).
Click Generate Track again.
Check the file is mp3 or wav (webm also accepted) and under 10 MB.
Click Clear if an old file is attached, then upload again.
Wait for 'Ready to generate' before generating.
Turn Instrumental off.
Type your lyrics in Prompt.
Click Generate Track.
Press Play again; the player reloads when the track changes.
Click Save to download the file and play it locally.
Generate again if the track still fails.

commonProblems.problem: Track is instrumental but I wanted a singer
commonProblems.whyItHappens: Instrumental is on by default for Suno Create Music.
commonProblems.howToFix: Turn Instrumental off and enter lyrics in Prompt.

commonProblems.problem: Cannot pick Suno V4 or V5.5
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The model-version dropdown is hidden in this studio and V5 is the default.
commonProblems.howToFix: Use the default; there is no version picker in the form.

commonProblems.problem: m4a file will not upload
commonProblems.whyItHappens: Only mp3, wav and webm audio pass the upload check, despite the on-screen hint.
commonProblems.howToFix: Convert to mp3 or wav under 10 MB.

commonProblems.problem: Alert says 20MB but my 15 MB file was refused
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The message text and the enforced limit differ; the enforced audio limit is 10 MB.
commonProblems.howToFix: Compress or trim the audio below 10 MB.

faqs.question: Where do I open Audio Studio?
faqs.answer: From the Audio Studio tab, route /studio/audio.

faqs.question: Which model should I start with?
faqs.answer: The Audio Model dropdown starts on Suno Create Music, which only requires Style. For spoken audio choose a speech model such as Minimax Speech HD.

faqs.question: How do I get lyrics sung?
faqs.answer: Turn Instrumental off and type the lyrics in Prompt. The model hint says the prompt is used as the exact lyrics.

faqs.question: Can I choose the Suno version?
faqs.answer: Not in this studio form: the Model field is hidden and V5 is the default.

faqs.question: What audio files can I upload?
faqs.answer: Audio files through the upload boxes; the upload contract accepts mp3 (audio/mpeg), wav and webm audio up to 10 MB. The box hint mentions M4A and 20MB but the code does not accept m4a or more than 10 MB.

faqs.question: How do I download the result?
faqs.answer: Click Save in the player. It saves an .mp3 named after your Title (or generated_audio.mp3).

faqs.question: Where are my previous results?
faqs.answer: In the Generation History grid at the bottom of the page; click a card to play it. It keeps up to 30 items in your browser.

faqs.question: Does it show what a generation will cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, an Estimated cost line above Generate Track, shown as 'calculating…' while updating or a dash if unavailable.

faqs.question: What does New Generation do?
faqs.answer: It returns to the settings view and keeps your parameters so you can adjust them.

faqs.question: Generation is blocked, what do I check?
faqs.answer: Open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

studios.shortDescription: Upload a long video (or paste a link to one), choose an aspect ratio and how many highlights you want, and get back short highlight clips, or only timing coordinates if you switch on Coordinates Only.
studios.fullDescription: AI Clipping takes one source video and sends it, with your chosen aspect ratio, highlight count and the Coordinates Only setting, to the MuAPI ai-clipping service. In the default mode the result is a gallery of rendered highlight clips (Clips Gallery Mode) that you can preview, copy a link to, download or post. With Coordinates Only switched on you instead get a Highlights Timeline next to the original video player (Timeline Seek Mode), where each highlight shows a start and end time and clicking it jumps the player to that moment. Each run is kept in a Clipping History Runs list in your browser. The text box at the bottom of the studio accepts a pasted video link, and its text is not sent to the clipping service.
whenToUse: You have a long recording and want short highlight clips
You only need start and end times of highlight moments
You want several aspect ratios of the same source video by running it more than once
whenToUseAnother: Use Video Studio to generate new video from text or images
Use the social publishing modal (the post button on a clip) when you are ready to publish a clip
Use Lip Sync or Recast studios to change what is said or who appears in a video
studios.bestFor: Creators, social media managers and marketers who repurpose long recordings into short clips.

inputDetails.name: source video
inputDetails.description: The long video to clip. Add it with the video upload button (tooltip Upload source video), by dragging a video file onto that button, by choosing a video under Saved, or by pasting a link that starts with http:// or https:// into the bottom text box. Once added, a small preview with a x button (tooltip Clear video) replaces the upload button.

inputDetails.restrictions: Uploaded files over 100 MB are rejected before upload. Only files the browser reports as video are accepted. A pasted link is used as-is, so it should be a direct link to a video file that the clipping service can fetch.

inputDetails.restrictions: Only the six listed ratios are offered.

inputDetails.name: max highlights
inputDetails.description: How many highlights to request. The button shows the current count (for example 3 Highlights); its menu titled Max Highlights has a slider with the label Limit: and goes from 1 to 60 in steps of 1.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want more or fewer clips than the default of 3.
inputDetails.restrictions: Slider range is 1 to 60. The service decides how many clips it actually returns.

inputDetails.name: Coordinates Only
inputDetails.description: A toggle button. When on, the request asks the service to return timing coordinates instead of rendered clips (return_coordinates_only).
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want start and end times to use elsewhere, or to review where the highlights are on the original video.
inputDetails.restrictions: Off by default. In this mode no clip files are returned; results show on the Highlights Timeline.

inputDetails.name: prompt text box
inputDetails.description: The bottom text box with the placeholder Describe prompt / highlights to extract. A value that is only a link starting with http:// or https:// is moved into the source video slot and the box is cleared.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Mainly as a quick place to paste a video link.
inputDetails.restrictions: Other text typed here is not included in the clipping request (the request carries only the video URL, highlight count, aspect ratio and the coordinates flag).

modeExplanations.description: Default. After Generate, the main area shows the heading Extracted Video Clips and a grid of rendered clips labelled Clip #1, Clip #2 and so on. Clips preview silently when you hover over them.
modeExplanations.useCase: Getting finished short clips to download or post

modeExplanations.description: Used when Coordinates Only is on. The main area shows the Original Video Player and a Highlights Timeline list. Each entry shows its start and end time, duration, and a score if one is returned; clicking it seeks the player to the start and plays (Seek & Play).
modeExplanations.useCase: Finding highlight moments or copying times into another editing tool

studios.modelExplanations: There is no model picker in AI Clipping. The label AI Clipping in the bottom bar only identifies the service. The settings sent are the video URL, the Max Highlights number, the aspect ratio and whether Coordinates Only is on. The results page lists whatever the service returns, so the number of clips can differ from the number you requested.
howToSteps: Open AI Clipping: choose AI Clipping in the studio list, or go to /studio/clipping.

Add your source video using any one of these: click the video-camera upload button at the left of the bottom bar (tooltip Upload source video) and choose a video file of up to 100 MB; drag a video file onto that button; click Saved and choose a video under Videos in Your library; or paste a link that starts with http:// or https:// into the text box (it moves into the source slot automatically).
Check that a small video preview appears in the bottom bar. Use its x button (tooltip Clear video) if you chose the wrong video.
Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 9:16 at first) and pick one of 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, 4:3 or 3:4 from the Aspect Ratio menu.
Click the highlights button (it shows 3 Highlights at first). In the Max Highlights menu drag the Limit: slider between 1 and 60.
Optional: click Coordinates Only if you want only timing data and not rendered clips. It is off by default; the button is highlighted when on.
Click Generate. The button changes to Generating... until the service finishes; long videos can take a while.

When it finishes you see either Extracted Video Clips (default) or, with Coordinates Only, the Original Video Player and Highlights Timeline. Hover a clip to preview it, use Copy Link or Download on the hover buttons, or click a timeline entry (Seek & Play) to jump the player to that highlight.
Click Back to History to leave the result. Earlier runs appear under Clipping History Runs; click a card to reopen it.

advancedFeatureExplanations.explanation: Switch it on before clicking Generate to get a Highlights Timeline instead of rendered clips.
advancedFeatureExplanations.restrictions: No downloadable clips in this mode

advancedFeatureExplanations.explanation: Saved opens Your library with Videos so you can reuse an earlier upload or generated video as the source.
advancedFeatureExplanations.useCase: Re-clipping a video with different settings
advancedFeatureExplanations.restrictions: Only shown while no source video is set

outputDetails.description: Rendered short videos shown under Extracted Video Clips, each labelled Clip #n with the aspect ratio.
postGenerationActions: Hover a clip to preview it
Post this to a social network (publish button)
On small screens use the actions menu on the card (Copy link, Download)

outputDetails.description: In Coordinates Only mode, a Highlights Timeline of entries with start and end times (shown as minutes:seconds), duration and an optional score.
postGenerationActions: Click an entry to seek and play the Original Video Player
Back to History to return to the run list

exampleWorkflows.title: Webinar to vertical clips
steps: Open AI Clipping and upload the webinar recording (under 100 MB) with Upload source video.
Keep 9:16 and set the Limit: slider in Max Highlights to 5.
Click Generate.
Hover each clip under Extracted Video Clips to preview, then click Download on the ones you like.

exampleWorkflows.title: Find moments without rendering clips
steps: Add the video, then click Coordinates Only so it is highlighted.
Click Generate.
In the Highlights Timeline click each entry to Seek & Play the Original Video Player.
Note the start and end times for your own editing.

exampleWorkflows.title: Reuse a saved video at a different shape
steps: Click Saved and pick the video under Videos.
Open the aspect ratio button and choose 16:9.
Click Generate.
Compare with your earlier run by clicking Back to History and opening the older card.

tips: Try a first run with the default 3 highlights, then increase the Max Highlights slider if you need more.
Pick the aspect ratio before you click Generate; it is sent with the request.
Keep uploads under 100 MB; for bigger files trim or compress the video first.
Use Coordinates Only to review where highlights fall before spending time on clip files.
Your history stays in this browser only, so download clips you want to keep.

commonProblems.problem: An alert says Please upload a video or paste a video URL first. when I click Generate
commonProblems.whyItHappens: No source video is set.
commonProblems.howToFix: Upload a video, choose one under Saved, or paste an http:// or https:// video link, then click Generate again.

commonProblems.problem: My file will not upload
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The file is over 100 MB, or is not recognised as a video.
commonProblems.howToFix: Compress or trim the video to under 100 MB and try again, or paste a link to a hosted copy.

commonProblems.problem: Typing in the text box does nothing to my clips
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The text box text is not sent to the clipping service; only a pasted link is used.
commonProblems.howToFix: Use the aspect ratio, Max Highlights and Coordinates Only settings to steer the result.

commonProblems.problem: Clicking a clip card does not open a bigger player
commonProblems.whyItHappens: Clip cards play a muted preview on hover.
commonProblems.howToFix: Hover over the card to preview it, or use Download to watch the full file.

commonProblems.problem: The timeline shows entries called Highlight #1, Highlight #2 with 15-second steps
commonProblems.whyItHappens: If Coordinates Only returns no coordinates, the studio fills in placeholder entries (Highlight #n, each 15 seconds long, one after another).
commonProblems.howToFix: Treat those times as placeholders and run again, or switch Coordinates Only off to get rendered clips.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Generate does nothing except show an alert
steps: Check that a video preview is visible in the bottom bar.
If not, upload a video, choose one under Saved, or paste a direct video link.
Click Generate again.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Upload failed or file too large
steps: Check the file is a video and under 100 MB.
Trim or compress it, then upload again.
Or paste a link to a hosted copy of the video into the text box.
Read the red error message in the bottom-right corner (it stays about 7 seconds).
If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
Try again with a smaller or shorter video, or a direct video link.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: No clips or highlights in the result
steps: The result shows No video clips generated. Try re-running. or No highlights extracted.
Click Back to History and click Generate again.
Try a different video or a different Max Highlights value.

limitationDetails.limitation: Uploaded video files are limited to 100 MB
limitationDetails.impact: Larger files are rejected with a size message before upload.
limitationDetails.workaround: Trim or compress the video, or paste a link to a hosted copy.

limitationDetails.limitation: Generation needs your own MuAPI key
limitationDetails.impact: Without a valid key generation is blocked.
limitationDetails.workaround: Open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

limitationDetails.limitation: The bottom text box does not steer the clips
limitationDetails.impact: Descriptions you type are not sent with the request.
limitationDetails.workaround: Use aspect ratio, Max Highlights and Coordinates Only.

limitationDetails.limitation: History is local to this browser
limitationDetails.impact: Past runs are saved in browser storage (up to 30) and do not follow you to another browser.
limitationDetails.workaround: Download the clips you want to keep.

limitationDetails.limitation: Clip cards have no fullscreen player
limitationDetails.impact: Clicking a card does not open a larger view.
limitationDetails.workaround: Hover to preview or download the file.

faqs.question: Where do I open AI Clipping?
faqs.answer: Choose AI Clipping in the studio list, or go to /studio/clipping.

faqs.question: How big can my video be?
faqs.answer: Files you upload can be up to 100 MB. Larger files are rejected with a message.

faqs.question: Can I paste a link instead of uploading?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paste a link that starts with http:// or https:// into the bottom text box and it becomes the source video. Use a direct link to a video file.

faqs.question: How many highlights can I ask for?
faqs.answer: From 1 to 60 using the Limit: slider in the Max Highlights menu. The default is 3.

faqs.question: Which aspect ratios are available?
What does Coordinates Only do?
faqs.answer: It asks for timing coordinates instead of rendered clips and shows them in a Highlights Timeline next to the Original Video Player. No clip files are returned in that mode.

faqs.question: Does the text I type in the bottom box change the clips?
faqs.answer: No. Only the video link, highlight count, aspect ratio and Coordinates Only setting are sent.

faqs.question: Where are my past runs?
faqs.answer: Click Back to History to see Clipping History Runs. They are saved in this browser only, up to 30 runs.

faqs.question: How do I download a clip?
faqs.answer: Hover over the clip card and click Download (or use the actions menu on small screens). The file is saved as an .mp4.

faqs.question: My generation failed. What should I check?
faqs.answer: Read the error message that appears at the bottom right. If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key. Then retry with a smaller video or a direct video link.

studios.businessValue: AI Clipping reduces the time spent scrubbing through long videos by returning highlight clips or highlight times from one request. You choose the output shape and how many highlights to ask for, and everything is reviewed in the same screen.
studios.competitivePositioning: AI Clipping is a single-purpose studio: one source video in, highlight clips or timing coordinates out, with a simple aspect ratio and highlight-count choice and no timeline editor. Use it for quick repurposing and move to an editor for fine control.
gettingStarted: Open AI Clipping from the studio list (/studio/clipping).
Add a video with the Upload source video button, drag and drop, Saved, or by pasting an http:// or https:// video link into the text box.
Leave the aspect ratio at 9:16 and the Max Highlights at 3 for a first test, or change them from the two buttons in the bottom bar.
Click Generate and wait while the button shows Generating...
Review the Extracted Video Clips, then use Copy Link or Download on the clips you want to keep.
Try Coordinates Only next to see the Highlights Timeline.
bestPractices: Start with a short test video to confirm the settings, then run the full-length one.
Choose the aspect ratio that matches where you will post: 9:16 for vertical feeds, 16:9 for wide, 1:1 or 4:5 for feed posts.
Ask for a few more highlights than you need and pick the best in review.
Download or copy the link of each clip you plan to use right after the run.
If you paste a link, use a direct link to a video file rather than a web page.

studios.name: Vibe Motion

keyFeatures: Text prompt to motion graphic video
Aspect ratio choice: 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1 (default 16:9)
Duration choice: 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25 or 30 seconds (default 6s)
Generate / Edit toggle: remix an earlier generation by describing the change

To change a finished result, hover its card and click the remix button (tooltip Remix this generation), describe the change, and click Remix.

Remix needs a generation with saved animation code
Gallery is local to this browser and limited to 30 entries
No image or audio inputs

Remix does nothing useful or is unavailable
My earlier results are gone

studios.shortDescription: Describe an animated motion graphic in words (kinetic typography, data charts, logo reveals) and get a rendered video; then remix a finished result by describing what to change.
studios.fullDescription: Vibe Motion turns a text description into an animated motion graphic video. You write a prompt, choose an aspect ratio (16:9, 9:16 or 1:1) and a duration (5 to 30 seconds), and click Generate. Finished videos collect in a gallery in your browser. Each generation that returned an ID can be remixed: switch to Edit, pick the source generation, describe the change, and click Remix to produce a changed version. The loading screen notes that the graphic is rendered with React/Remotion on a remote service.
whenToUse: You want an animated chart, title or logo-style graphic from a text description
You want to adjust an existing motion graphic by describing the change
whenToUseAnother: Use Video Studio for generated video scenes from text or images
Use Motion Control Studio to copy motion from a reference video onto your character images
Use Cinema Studio for camera-directed footage
studios.bestFor: Creators and marketers who need short animated graphics, titles and charts from a text prompt.

featureExplanations.explanation: Two buttons in the bottom bar open menus. Both values are sent with every Generate or Remix request and shown on the card (for example 16:9 and 6s).
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Match the video to where it will be used.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Three ratios and nine durations only.

featureExplanations.explanation: Click Edit, pick a source under Source Generation (or use the remix button on a card), describe the change and click Remix.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Adjust an existing motion graphic without writing the whole prompt again.
featureExplanations.inputRequired: an earlier generation and a change description
featureExplanations.restrictions: Source must have an ID and saved animation code.

featureExplanations.explanation: Results appear as cards with a Generated or Edit tag, the prompt, the aspect ratio and duration. Hover to preview silently; click the card to open a fullscreen player.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Compare versions and reuse earlier results.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Up to 30 entries, stored in this browser only.

featureExplanations.explanation: Press Ctrl+Enter (or Cmd+Enter) inside the prompt box to run, same as the button. A hint reading Ctrl+Enter to run shows on wider screens.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Run without moving to the button.
featureExplanations.restrictions: Same rules as the button.

inputDetails.name: prompt
inputDetails.description: Text box at the bottom. In Generate mode its placeholder reads Describe the motion graphic with an example about an animated sales dashboard; in Edit mode it asks you to describe what to change.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Always. Generate stays disabled while the box is empty.
inputDetails.restrictions: Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. No character limit is set in the code.

inputDetails.name: aspect ratio
inputDetails.description: Button showing the current ratio (default 16:9). Its menu titled Aspect Ratio lists 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Choose before generating: 16:9 for wide video, 9:16 for vertical, 1:1 for square.
inputDetails.restrictions: Only these three options.

inputDetails.name: duration
inputDetails.description: Button showing the current length (default 6s). Its menu titled Duration lists 5s, 6s, 8s, 10s, 12s, 15s, 20s, 25s and 30s.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Longer graphics with more elements generally need a longer duration; this is your choice.
inputDetails.restrictions: Only these nine options.

inputDetails.name: source generation (Edit mode only)
inputDetails.description: In Edit mode a button (shows Pick source… until you choose) opens a menu titled Source Generation listing your earlier generations; the chosen one is shown in the banner as Editing: with the start of its prompt.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When remixing. You can also hover a card and click the remix button to set it automatically.
inputDetails.restrictions: Only generations that returned an ID are listed. Edit is disabled until you have at least one.

modeExplanations.description: Default mode. Your prompt is sent with the chosen aspect ratio and duration and a new motion graphic is created.
modeExplanations.useCase: Creating a new motion graphic

modeExplanations.description: Remix mode. Your prompt is treated as a description of what to change in a selected earlier generation. The button changes to Remix.
modeExplanations.useCase: Changing colours, background or elements of an existing result

studios.modelExplanations: There is no model picker in this studio. The loading screen states that the graphic is rendered with React/Remotion on a remote service. A remix only works for a generation whose animation code was saved by that service; older or unsupported results show a message and Edit mode is turned off.
howToSteps: Open Vibe Motion: choose Vibe Motion in the studio list, or go to /studio/vibe-motion.
Make sure the Generate option is selected at the top of the bottom bar (it is the default).
Click the prompt box and describe the motion graphic, for example an animated sales dashboard with glowing bar charts and rising numbers.
Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 16:9 at first) and choose 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1 from the Aspect Ratio menu.
Click the duration button (it shows 6s at first) and choose a length from 5s up to 30s in the Duration menu.
Click Generate (or press Ctrl+Enter). The button changes to Generating... and a Generating motion graphics… screen shows a running timer.
When it finishes, the result appears as a card in the gallery. Hover over it to preview, or click it to watch it fullscreen.
To save the video, hover the card and click the download button (tooltip Download).

To change a result: hover its card and click the remix button (tooltip Remix this generation), or click Edit and pick it under Pick source…. Describe what to change in the prompt box and click Remix (it shows Remixing... while it works). The new version is added to the gallery with an Edit tag.
To leave Edit mode without remixing, click the x on the banner (tooltip Cancel Edit Mode) or click Generate in the toggle.

advancedFeatureExplanations.explanation: Turns an earlier generation into a new version using a text description of the change.
advancedFeatureExplanations.restrictions: Only generations with saved animation code can be remixed

advancedFeatureExplanations.explanation: Click a card to open the video in a large player; click the x or outside the video to close it.
advancedFeatureExplanations.restrictions: none

outputDetails.description: A video (downloaded as .mp4) shown as a card in the gallery with its prompt, aspect ratio and duration.
postGenerationActions: Post this to a social network (publish button)

steps: Hover the finished card and click the remix button (Remix this generation).
Type: change background to dark navy, make bars gold.
Click Remix.
Compare the new card (Edit tag) with the original.

tips: Be concrete: name the elements, colours, background and movement you want in the prompt.
For a remix, describe only the change, for example the background colour or an added element.
Pick 9:16 for vertical video and 1:1 for square before you generate.
Use a short duration (5s or 6s) for a first test.
Download results you want to keep: the gallery is stored in this browser only.

commonProblems.problem: Generate is greyed out
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The prompt box is empty (or, in Edit mode, no source generation is selected).
commonProblems.howToFix: Type a description; in Edit mode pick a source under Pick source… (until you do, the banner says Select a source generation from the gallery) or use the remix button on a card.

commonProblems.problem: The Edit option is disabled
commonProblems.whyItHappens: There is no earlier generation with an ID in your gallery yet.
commonProblems.howToFix: Click Generate to create a motion graphic first, then use Edit.

commonProblems.problem: A message says the generation can not be remixed
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The service did not keep the animation code for that generation.
commonProblems.howToFix: Generate a new motion graphic and remix that one instead. The studio returns to Generate mode automatically.

commonProblems.problem: The remix button on a card is missing
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The hover buttons show only on larger screens, and only generations with an ID can be remixed.
commonProblems.howToFix: On a small screen use the actions menu on the card (Remix). Otherwise use Edit and Pick source….

steps: Read the error message shown at the top right.
If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
Click Generate again, or try a shorter duration or simpler prompt.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Remix does nothing useful or is unavailable
steps: Check you have chosen a source under Pick source… (the banner shows Editing: followed by its prompt).
Type what to change in the prompt box.
If you see the message about animation code not being saved, generate a new graphic and remix that.
The gallery is stored in this browser. Check you are in the same browser and signed in with the same key.
Download results you want to keep.

limitationDetails.limitation: Remix needs a generation with saved animation code

limitationDetails.workaround: Generate a new graphic and remix that.

limitationDetails.limitation: Gallery is local to this browser and limited to 30 entries

studios.name: Lip Sync Studio
studios.description: Makes a talking video by syncing an audio track to a portrait image or to an existing video, with a choice of lip-sync and avatar models for each of the two input modes.
keyFeatures: Two input modes: "Portrait Image" (image + audio) and "Video" (video + audio)
Model dropdown that changes with the mode (portrait/avatar models in Portrait Image mode, video lip-sync models in Video mode)
Resolution dropdown that appears only when the selected model offers resolution choices (480p, 720p, 1080p depending on the model)
Optional text box ("Describe speech style...") sent only to models that accept a prompt
Upload from your computer, drag and drop, or pick from the shared "Library" of saved uploads and generations
Gallery of your recent results with hover preview, full-screen view, copy prompt, Download, Post to social and Delete
studios.howToUse: 1. Open Lip Sync Studio at /studio/lipsync (the "Lip Sync" tab in the studio tab bar). The bar at the bottom of the page holds all the controls. 2. Choose the input mode with the two buttons at the top of the bottom bar: "Portrait Image" (a still face plus audio) or "Video" (an existing video plus audio). "Portrait Image" is selected when you first open the studio. 3. Add your picture or video: click the round upload button (it opens a file picker), or drag a file onto it, or click "Library" and pick a saved file. Images must be under 10MB and videos under 50MB. The upload accepts JPG, PNG and WEBP images and MP4, WEBM and MOV videos. 4. Add your audio: click the microphone button (or drag an audio file onto it, or choose one from "Library"). Audio must be under 10MB; the upload accepts MP3, WAV and WEBM audio. Once uploaded, click the audio button to play or pause it, and click the small x on its corner to remove it. 5. Click the model button (it shows the current model name, or "Select model") and choose a model from the "Model" list. Switching mode resets the model to the first model of that mode. 6. If a resolution button appears next to the model button, click it and choose a size from the "Resolution" list. Models without a resolution choice do not show this button. 7. Optionally type a note in the text box (placeholder "Describe speech style..."). It is only used by models that accept a prompt; other models ignore it. 8. Click "Sync Lip". The button changes to "Generating..." until the video is ready. 9. When it finishes, the new video appears at the top of the gallery above the bar. Hover over it to preview, click it to open it full screen, and use the icons that appear on hover to copy the prompt, download it ("Download"), post it to social or delete it ("Delete").
studios.modelCapabilities: The Model dropdown lists different models in each mode. Portrait Image mode lists Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2 Speech to Video, LTX 2.3 Lipsync, LTX 2 19B Lipsync, Kling v1 and v2 Avatar (Standard and Pro) and Omnihuman 1 5. Video mode lists Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify Lipsync, Veed Lipsync, Infinite Talk V2V and Volcengine Video to Video Lip Sync. Each entry shows a short description in the dropdown.
limitations: Upload size limits
Accepted file types
Only the current mode's input is kept
Gallery length
Audio length
troubleshooting: Nothing happens or a toast says "Please upload an audio file first.": Upload an audio file with the microphone button (or pick one from "Library").
Toast says "Please upload a portrait image first." or "Please upload a source video first.": Check which mode is selected at the top of the bottom bar.
Upload fails or is refused: Check the size: images and audio under 10MB, videos under 50MB.
Generation fails: Try a shorter audio clip or a different model.
No resolution button is visible: This is expected: only some models offer a resolution choice.

studios.shortDescription: Turn a portrait image or an existing video, plus an audio file, into a lip-synced talking video.
studios.fullDescription: Lip Sync Studio (the "Lip Sync" tab) has two input modes, "Portrait Image" and "Video". In Portrait Image mode you upload a still face image and an audio file and a model animates the face to speak that audio; the model list for this mode includes Infinite Talk, Wan 2.2 Speech to Video, LTX lipsync models, Kling avatar models and Omnihuman. In Video mode you upload an existing video and an audio file and a model re-syncs the speaker's mouth to the new audio; the list for this mode includes Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify, Veed, Infinite Talk V2V and a Volcengine model. You pick a model from a dropdown, optionally pick a resolution (only shown for models that offer one) and optionally type a short note in the text box (only sent to models that accept a prompt). Click "Sync Lip" and the finished video appears at the top of the gallery on the same page, where you can play it, open it full screen, download it, post it to social or delete it.
whenToUse: You have a still image and a voice recording and want a talking video
You have footage and want to change what the speaker says
You want an avatar-style narrator from an image
whenToUseAnother: Use Audio Studio to create or clone the voice first
Use Video Studio for general video generation from text or images
Use Marketing Studio for product ads with avatars
studios.bestFor: Anyone who needs a speaking face from an image or a re-synced video, without filming.

howToSteps: Open Lip Sync Studio at /studio/lipsync (the "Lip Sync" tab in the studio tab bar). The bar at the bottom of the page holds all the controls.

Choose the input mode with the two buttons at the top of the bottom bar: "Portrait Image" (a still face plus audio) or "Video" (an existing video plus audio). "Portrait Image" is selected when you first open the studio.

Add your picture or video: click the round upload button (it opens a file picker), or drag a file onto it, or click "Library" and pick a saved file. Images must be under 10MB and videos under 50MB. The upload accepts JPG, PNG and WEBP images and MP4, WEBM and MOV videos.

Add your audio: click the microphone button (or drag an audio file onto it, or choose one from "Library"). Audio must be under 10MB; the upload accepts MP3, WAV and WEBM audio. Once uploaded, click the audio button to play or pause it, and click the small x on its corner to remove it.
Click the model button (it shows the current model name, or "Select model") and choose a model from the "Model" list. Switching mode resets the model to the first model of that mode.
If a resolution button appears next to the model button, click it and choose a size from the "Resolution" list. Models without a resolution choice do not show this button.
Optionally type a note in the text box (placeholder "Describe speech style..."). It is only used by models that accept a prompt; other models ignore it.
Click "Sync Lip". The button changes to "Generating..." until the video is ready.

When it finishes, the new video appears at the top of the gallery above the bar. Hover over it to preview, click it to open it full screen, and use the icons that appear on hover to copy the prompt, download it ("Download"), post it to social or delete it ("Delete").

exampleWorkflows.title: Talking head from a photo
steps: Open /studio/lipsync and keep "Portrait Image" selected.
Upload a front-facing portrait with the image button.
Upload your narration with the microphone button.
Leave the default model, or choose another from the "Model" list.
Click "Sync Lip" and wait for the video to appear in the gallery.
Hover over the card and click Download.

exampleWorkflows.title: Replace the voice in an existing clip
steps: Open /studio/lipsync and click "Video".
Upload the clip (under 50MB).
Upload the new audio (under 10MB).
Choose a model such as Sync Lipsync from the "Model" list.
Click "Sync Lip".
Open the result from the gallery to check the mouth movement.

exampleWorkflows.title: Compare two models on the same inputs
steps: Upload your image and audio in "Portrait Image" mode.
Click "Sync Lip" with the first model.
Open the "Model" list, choose a different model (set a resolution if the button appears).
Click "Sync Lip" again; your uploads are kept.
Compare the two cards in the gallery and download the better one.

exampleWorkflows.title: Reuse a saved file
steps: Open /studio/lipsync.
Click "Library" and choose a saved image (or audio) from the tabs.
Add any missing audio the same way.
Click "Sync Lip".

tips: Start with a short audio clip and the default model to check the result before running longer audio or a different model.
Use a clear, front-facing portrait with the whole face visible in Portrait Image mode.
Use clean audio with little background noise so the mouth movement follows the speech clearly.
Resolution and model are independent: if a model offers 480p, 720p or 1080p, the default is shown on the button, so check it before you generate.
Your uploads, selected model, resolution, text and recent results are remembered in your browser between visits, so you can leave and come back.
Use the text box only with models that accept a prompt; it has no effect on the video-to-video models such as Sync Lipsync, LatentSync, Creatify, Veed or Volcengine.

commonProblems.problem: My audio is rejected

commonProblems.howToFix: Convert the audio to MP3 or WAV and keep it under 10MB.

Click "Sync Lip" again.

Click "Sync Lip" again.

limitationDetails.impact: A file over the limit is refused with "Image exceeds 10MB limit.", "Video exceeds 50MB limit." or "Audio file exceeds 10MB limit."
limitationDetails.workaround: Compress or trim the file and upload again.

limitationDetails.impact: The upload accepts JPG, PNG and WEBP images, MP4, WEBM and MOV videos, and MP3, WAV and WEBM audio. Other formats (for example M4A, OGG, FLAC, AVIF or GIF) are rejected with an "Invalid file type" message.
limitationDetails.workaround: Convert the file to a supported format first.

limitationDetails.limitation: Only the current mode's input is kept
limitationDetails.impact: Switching between "Portrait Image" and "Video" clears the image or video you uploaded and resets the model.
limitationDetails.workaround: Switch mode first, then upload.

limitationDetails.impact: The gallery keeps your 30 most recent results in this browser.
limitationDetails.workaround: Download results you want to keep.

limitationDetails.impact: No audio length limit is shown in the studio; any limit is set by the selected model.
limitationDetails.workaround: Try a short clip first.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Portrait Image and Video mode?
faqs.answer: Portrait Image mode animates a still face image so it speaks your audio. Video mode takes an existing video and re-syncs the speaker's mouth to your audio.

faqs.question: What file types and sizes can I upload?
faqs.answer: Images up to 10MB (JPG, PNG, WEBP), videos up to 50MB (MP4, WEBM, MOV) and audio up to 10MB (MP3, WAV, WEBM). Larger or other types are refused.

faqs.question: Why is there no Resolution button?
faqs.answer: The Resolution button only appears for models that offer a resolution choice. Choose a different model if you need one.

faqs.question: Does the text box change the result?
faqs.answer: Only for models that accept a prompt. The video-to-video lip-sync models ignore it.

faqs.question: Where does my finished video go?
faqs.answer: To the top of the gallery on the same page. It stays in your browser; the gallery keeps the 30 most recent results, so download anything you want to keep.

faqs.question: Can I reuse a file I uploaded earlier?
faqs.answer: Yes. Click "Library" and pick it from the tabs. In Portrait Image mode the tabs are Images and Audio; in Video mode they are Videos and Audio.

faqs.question: How do I remove an uploaded file?
faqs.answer: Click the small x on the corner of the upload button. For image and video, clicking the button itself also clears it; for audio, clicking the button plays or pauses it.

faqs.question: Can I drag and drop files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Drop a file onto the matching upload button. Files dropped onto the studio are also picked up: audio fills the audio slot, a video switches to Video mode and an image switches to Portrait Image mode.

faqs.question: How do I download a result?
faqs.answer: Hover over the result card in the gallery and click the Download icon (tooltip "Download"). On small screens use the actions menu on the card.

faqs.question: Why do I see a message about my MuAPI key?
faqs.answer: If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

studios.businessValue: Produces speaking-face videos from a picture or existing footage plus an audio file, so you can create or re-voice clips without a new shoot.
studios.competitivePositioning: Lip Sync Studio offers several lip-sync and avatar models behind one screen, with a single flow for image-driven and video-driven sync.
gettingStarted: Open Lip Sync Studio from the studio tab bar ("Lip Sync") or go to /studio/lipsync.
Pick "Portrait Image" if you have a still face, or "Video" if you want to change the speech in existing footage.
Upload your image or video, then upload your audio with the microphone button.
Choose a model (and a resolution if that button is shown).
Click "Sync Lip" and wait for the video to appear at the top of the gallery.
Download it, post it to social, or keep generating variations with a different model.
bestPractices: Convert audio to MP3 or WAV before uploading, because the upload rejects other audio types.
Keep images under 10MB, videos under 50MB and audio under 10MB; the studio refuses larger files before uploading.
Use Video mode when you already have footage of the speaker and only want to change the spoken audio; use Portrait Image mode when you only have a still image.
Compare two models on the same short clip before committing to a long one.
Download results you want to keep; the gallery lists only your 30 most recent results.

studios.name: Cinema Studio
studios.description: Generates cinematic still images from a text description, with a camera body, lens, focal length and aperture that you choose in a Camera settings panel.
keyFeatures: Text-to-image with a cinematic prompt: your text plus the chosen camera, lens, focal length and aperture
"Camera settings" panel with four scrolling columns: Camera, Lens, Focal length, Aperture
Six camera bodies and eleven lenses to choose from, focal lengths 8, 14, 24, 35, 50 and 85 mm, apertures f/1.4, f/4 and f/11
Aspect ratios 16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5; resolutions 1K, 2K and 4K
Optional single reference image (upload, drag and drop, or "Library")
Gallery with full-screen view, copy prompt, copy image, Download, Post to social and Delete
studios.howToUse: 1. Open Cinema Studio at /studio/cinema (the "Cinema Studio" tab in the studio tab bar). The controls are in the bar at the bottom of the page. 2. Type your scene in the text box (placeholder "Describe your cinema scene..."). The "Shoot" button stays disabled until the box has text. 3. Optional: add a reference image. Click the round picture button at the left of the text box to choose a file, drag an image onto it, or click "Library" to reuse a saved image. Click the picture again (an x appears on hover) to remove it. 4. Click the aspect ratio button (it shows 16:9 at first) and choose from the "Aspect Ratio" list: 16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1 or 4:5. 5. Click the resolution button (it shows 2K at first) and choose from the "Resolution" list: 1K, 2K or 4K. 6. Click the camera summary button at the right of the controls (it reads like "Modular 8K Digital · Creative Tilt Lens, 35mm, f/1.4"). The "Camera settings" panel opens. 7. In the panel, scroll or drag each of the four columns, "Camera", "Lens", "Focal length" and "Aperture", until the option you want sits in the highlighted middle row; clicking an option also scrolls it into place. Close the panel with the Close button at the top right, with the Escape key, or by clicking outside it. 8. Click "Shoot". The button shows "Generating..." while the image is made. 9. The new image appears at the top of the gallery. Click it to open it full screen. Hover over a card to show the action icons: copy prompt, copy image, "Download", Post to social, an AI assist star and "Delete".
studios.modelCapabilities: Cinema Studio has no model picker. It uses one image model for text-only shots and the matching edit model when a reference image is attached.
limitations: Images only
One reference image
No model choice
Silent upload failures
Gallery length
Fixed negative wording
troubleshooting: The "Shoot" button is disabled: Type a scene description into the box.
The reference image does not attach: Check that the file is a JPG, PNG or WEBP under 10MB.
Generation fails: Click "Shoot" again.
Copy image does not work: Image copy needs a secure page (HTTPS or localhost).
My previous shot is gone from the gallery: The gallery keeps only the 50 most recent shots in this browser.

studios.shortDescription: Describe a scene, choose a camera, lens, focal length and aperture, and shoot a cinematic still image.
studios.fullDescription: Cinema Studio produces still images, not video. You type a scene description, optionally add one reference image, pick an aspect ratio and a resolution (1K, 2K or 4K), and open the camera summary button to choose a camera body, a lens, a focal length and an aperture in the "Camera settings" panel. When you click "Shoot", the studio adds your camera choices and some fixed quality wording to your text and generates the image. With a reference image attached it edits or builds on that image; without one it generates from text alone. Results are added to a gallery on the same page, where you can open them full screen, copy the prompt or the image, download, post to social or delete them.
whenToUse: You want a cinematic-looking still from text
You want to control camera, lens, focal length and aperture
You want to rework one existing image
whenToUseAnother: Use Video Studio for motion
Use Image Studio to choose a specific image model or use several reference images
Use Storyboard to plan a sequence of shots
studios.bestFor: Creators who want film-style stills and key art with camera-style controls.

Close the panel with the Close button at the top right, with the Escape key, or by clicking outside it.
Click "Shoot". The button shows "Generating..." while the image is made.

The new image appears at the top of the gallery. Click it to open it full screen. Hover over a card to show the action icons: copy prompt, copy image, "Download", Post to social, an AI assist star and "Delete".

faqs.question: Does Cinema Studio make video?
faqs.answer: No. It generates still images. Use Video Studio to turn an image into video.

faqs.question: Where do I choose the camera and lens?
faqs.answer: Click the camera summary button on the bottom bar. The "Camera settings" panel has columns for "Camera", "Lens", "Focal length" and "Aperture".

faqs.question: Which aspect ratios and resolutions are available?
faqs.answer: Aspect ratios 16:9, 21:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5 (default 16:9). Resolutions 1K, 2K and 4K (default 2K).

faqs.question: Can I choose the image model?
faqs.answer: No. The studio picks a text-to-image model, or an edit model when a reference image is attached.

faqs.question: Why is the Shoot button grey?
faqs.answer: It is disabled while the text box is empty or while a shot is being generated.

faqs.question: How many reference images can I add?

faqs.question: How do I download or copy a result?
faqs.answer: Hover over the card in the gallery and use the icons: "Copy prompt", "Copy image", "Download", Post to social, an AI assist star and "Delete". On small screens the same actions are in a menu on the card.

faqs.question: Are my shots saved?
faqs.answer: Your recent shots, settings and text are kept in your browser (up to 50 shots), so they are still there when you return in the same browser.

faqs.question: Can I start from a template or a storyboard?
faqs.answer: Yes: a template from the landing page or a hand-off from Storyboard can fill in the prompt and aspect ratio when you open the studio.

faqs.question: Why do I see a message about my MuAPI key?
faqs.answer: If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
