studios.name: Storyboard
studios.shortDescription: Plan a short film as scenes with camera settings and characters, draw a still frame for each scene, export the board as JSON, PDF or an animated GIF, or render it as one storyboard video.
studios.fullDescription: Storyboard is a planning studio. You write a project name and a creative brief, split the brief into scenes, give each scene a length and optional camera settings, tag the characters that appear in it, and draw a still frame for each scene. You can then export the board (JSON, PDF, or an animated GIF of the frames), generate one storyboard video from all the scenes with the Generate Storyboard button, or send the board to Video Studio, Cinema Studio or VFX Studio. Scene frames can be drawn by a MuAPI image model or by OpenAI image models (using your own OpenAI key from Settings); the OpenAI option also lets you edit a frame with a text instruction and guide the layout with a rough sketch. Your projects are kept in this browser.
keyFeatures: Several projects at once: a PROJECT switcher with New and Delete
Creative brief that can be split into one scene per line or sentence with Brief → scenes
Scene list with a length per scene and a running total against the clip length (5s or 10s)
Characters with a name, traits and an uploaded or pasted reference image, tagged onto scenes
Per-scene camera settings: shot type, angle, movement, camera, lens, focal length, aperture
A still frame per scene from a MuAPI image model or from OpenAI image models (Frame engine)
OpenAI panels: Edit a frame with a text instruction and add a Sketch to steer the composition
Drag scenes to reorder them
Export as JSON, PDF (browser print dialog) or an animated GIF of the generated frames
Generate Storyboard: one storyboard video from all scenes
Send to Video Studio, Cinema Studio or VFX Studio
Scene Analysis page with counts and a scene breakdown
studios.howToUse: Open Storyboard from the studio list (route /studio/storyboard). On the Storyboard page type a PROJECT NAME and CREATIVE BRIEF, pick the ASPECT RATIO and CLIP LENGTH, add scenes (Quick-add a scene or Brief → scenes), optionally add Characters, then open Shot Editor to set camera options and draw a still frame for each scene. Back on the Storyboard page use Generate Storyboard to make the storyboard video, or export with JSON, PDF or Send to.
howToSteps: Open Storyboard from the studio list. The Storyboard page opens with a PROJECT bar at the top; click New to start a fresh project, or choose an existing one in the project drop-down.
In 1. Project & Creative Brief, type a PROJECT NAME (the placeholder reads My Animated Series) and describe the story in CREATIVE BRIEF, one line per scene works best.
Choose the ASPECT RATIO (16:9 or 9:16) and the CLIP LENGTH (5s or 10s).

Click Brief → scenes to create one scene for each line (or each sentence, if the brief is a single paragraph). You can also type a scene into Quick-add a scene… and click Add. Each scene starts with a length; the page shows the total against the clip length and a Fit to button if they do not match.
Optional: in the Characters box, enter a Name, Traits and a reference image (use Upload or paste a URL), then click Add Character. Characters are tagged onto scenes later.

Click Shot Editor. For each scene you can edit the text, set its length in seconds, tag characters, and open Camera to choose SHOT TYPE, ANGLE, MOVEMENT, CAMERA, LENS, FOCAL and APERTURE (each one can stay on Any).
In Shot Editor choose the FRAME ENGINE: MuAPI (pick the image model with the model button at the top right) or OpenAI Images (pick the OpenAI image model and Panel detail).

Click Frame on a scene to draw its still frame. The button changes to Regenerate once a frame exists. With OpenAI Images you can also add a Sketch before generating, and use the Change this frame box with Edit after a frame exists.
Drag the handle on a scene card to reorder scenes.
To save the board, go back to the Storyboard page and use JSON or PDF at the top right. To make an animated preview, set seconds per frame in the ANIMATED GIF row of Shot Editor and click Export GIF.
To render a video from all scenes, click Generate Storyboard in 3. Generate Storyboard Video and wait for the player to appear. Use Send to to continue in Video Studio, Cinema Studio or VFX Studio.
gettingStarted: Open Storyboard from the studio list (it opens on the Storyboard page).
Type a PROJECT NAME and a CREATIVE BRIEF with one line per scene.
Pick ASPECT RATIO and CLIP LENGTH, then click Brief → scenes.
Open Shot Editor and click Frame on a scene to see your first still frame.
Come back to the Storyboard page and click Generate Storyboard when the scenes are ready.
tips: Write the brief one line per scene; Brief → scenes then gives you a ready scene list.
Keep the scene lengths close to the clip length. If the total is off, the page shows a warning and a Fit to button that rescales every scene.
Add a reference image to each character; it is sent with every scene where that character is tagged so the character stays recognisable.
Use OpenAI Images when you want to refine one frame: type what to change in the Change this frame box and click Edit.
Choose a low Panel detail (Low detail (fastest)) while testing ideas and a higher one for final frames.
Export GIF needs at least one generated frame; only scenes that already have a frame are included.
bestPractices: Plan the story first (brief and scenes), then add characters, then draw frames; frames use the scene text, tagged characters and camera settings.
Use one aspect ratio per project. The aspect ratio you choose on the Storyboard page is used for frames, the GIF and the video.
Draw frames one scene at a time and use Regenerate until you are happy, then export.
Use the PROJECT switcher to keep separate stories apart; each project keeps its own scenes and characters.

inputDetails.name: project name
inputDetails.description: The name of the storyboard (PROJECT NAME). It is used in export file names.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Always useful so projects can be told apart.
inputDetails.restrictions: Free text.

inputDetails.name: creative brief
inputDetails.description: The story described beat by beat (CREATIVE BRIEF). Brief → scenes turns it into scenes.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want scenes created automatically from a text.
inputDetails.restrictions: One line per scene works best. A single paragraph is split by sentence.

inputDetails.name: aspect ratio
inputDetails.description: 16:9 or 9:16 buttons under ASPECT RATIO.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Before drawing frames or generating the video.
inputDetails.restrictions: Only 16:9 and 9:16 are offered.

inputDetails.name: clip length
inputDetails.description: The target length of the storyboard video: 5s or 10s (CLIP LENGTH).
inputDetails.whenToUse: Before generating the storyboard video.
inputDetails.restrictions: Only 5s and 10s are offered. The scene lengths should add up to it.

inputDetails.name: scene
inputDetails.description: A scene description with a length in seconds.
inputDetails.whenToUse: At least one scene is needed to generate frames, export or generate the storyboard video.
inputDetails.restrictions: Quick-add starts at 3 seconds. The length field accepts 0 to 10 in steps of 0.5.

inputDetails.name: character
inputDetails.description: A named character with Traits and a reference image, attached to scenes.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When the same person or creature appears in several scenes.
inputDetails.restrictions: A name is required to add a character. Reference upload accepts PNG, JPEG or WebP, or paste an image URL.

inputDetails.name: camera settings
inputDetails.description: Per-scene SHOT TYPE, ANGLE, MOVEMENT, CAMERA, LENS, FOCAL and APERTURE; each can stay on Any.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When a scene needs a specific look or camera move.
inputDetails.restrictions: The choices are added to the text of the scene as plain words for the image or video model.

inputDetails.name: frame engine
inputDetails.description: MuAPI or OpenAI Images, chosen in Shot Editor.
inputDetails.whenToUse: MuAPI for the normal image model list; OpenAI Images for frame edits, sketches and detail levels.
inputDetails.restrictions: OpenAI Images uses your own OpenAI key from Settings. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

inputDetails.name: sketch
inputDetails.description: A rough drawing or reference image added to one scene with the Sketch button (OpenAI Images only).
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want the frame to follow a particular layout.
inputDetails.restrictions: Image files only, 2.5 MB at most. It is not saved with the project, and at most 4 reference images are sent with a frame.

inputDetails.name: frame edit instruction
inputDetails.description: A short text typed in the Change this frame box (OpenAI Images only).
inputDetails.whenToUse: To change an existing frame, for example make it night.
inputDetails.restrictions: Needs an existing frame.

studios.modelCapabilities: Frames can be drawn by a MuAPI image model (picked with the model button in Shot Editor, which opens a list with a Search models... box and provider filter) or, when FRAME ENGINE is OpenAI Images, by an OpenAI image model chosen in the OpenAI image model drop-down. The storyboard video is generated by the storyboard video service from the scene list, clip length, aspect ratio and (if present) the first character reference image.
studios.modelExplanations: Two engines draw scene frames. MuAPI uses the model chosen with the model button at the top right of Shot Editor and sends the reference images of tagged characters along. OpenAI Images uses an OpenAI image model chosen in the OpenAI image model drop-down plus a Panel detail setting (Low detail (fastest), Medium detail, High detail); it also supports Edit and Sketch. The on-screen hint says the faster option is for trying ideas and the more detailed one is better for busy scenes. The storyboard video uses its own service and only accepts a 5 or 10 second clip.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Generate Storyboard does nothing or shows a plan message
steps: Make sure there is at least one scene with text.
If you see 'An active plan is required to generate storyboards.', check that your plan is active.
If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
Confirm the scene has text; the Frame button is disabled for an empty scene.
With MuAPI, try another model with the model button at the top right of Shot Editor.
With OpenAI Images, if you see 'Add your OpenAI API key in Settings to generate storyboard panels.', add your OpenAI key in Settings.
Click Regenerate to try again.
Sketch and Edit only appear when FRAME ENGINE is set to OpenAI Images.
The Change this frame box also needs a generated frame.
Generate at least one frame first; the button title says 'Generate at least one frame first'.
Allow pop-ups for the site; if they are blocked an HTML file is downloaded instead.
In the print dialog choose the PDF option.

steps: The project bar and the Shot Editor and Analysis buttons are locked while a storyboard video is generating; wait for it to finish.

commonProblems.problem: Scene lengths do not add up to the clip length

commonProblems.problem: Sketch rejected

commonProblems.problem: Character looks different between frames

commonProblems.howToFix: Open Shot Editor, click the character name under the scene to tag it, and add a reference image to the character.

commonProblems.problem: Reference image upload fails

commonProblems.howToFix: Use one of those types or paste an image URL into the reference field.

faqs.question: Where do I open Storyboard?
faqs.answer: From the studio list, at /studio/storyboard. It opens on the Storyboard page; Shot Editor and Analysis are reached with buttons in 2. Scenes.

faqs.question: Does Storyboard still have episodes?
faqs.answer: No. The current screens work with a project, a brief, scenes and characters; there is no episode screen.

faqs.question: How long can the clip be?
faqs.answer: CLIP LENGTH offers 5s and 10s only.

faqs.question: Which aspect ratios can I use?

faqs.question: Can I export an animated GIF?

faqs.question: How do I get a PDF?

faqs.question: Where are my projects saved?
faqs.answer: In this browser. Use JSON to keep a backup file.

faqs.question: Can I send the storyboard to another studio?

studios.name: Marketing Studio
studios.description: Creates a short video ad from your ad script, a product image, an optional avatar image, optional reference images and a video format preset.
keyFeatures: Ad script box that understands @image1 (product) and @image2 (avatar) placeholders
Three upload slots: Product (required), Avatar and References (up to six images)
"Video Format Presets": UGC, Tutorial, Unboxing, Hyper Motion, Product Review, TV Spot
"Avatar Presets": Priya, Elena, Kai, Sora, Minji, Margot, Niko and Jin, with an enlarge preview
Aspect ratio 9:16, 3:4, 4:3, 16:9 or 1:1; resolution 720p or 1080p; duration 4 to 15 seconds
Opens the finished ad full screen and keeps results in a gallery with Download, Post to social and Delete
studios.howToUse: 1. Open Marketing Studio at /studio/marketing (the "Marketing Studio" tab in the studio tab bar). The controls are in the bar at the bottom of the page. 2. Type your ad script in the large text box (placeholder "Describe your ad script... Use @image1 for product, @image2 for avatar."). Use @image1 to refer to the product image and @image2 to refer to the avatar image. 3. Upload your product image with the first round button in the row of upload buttons (tooltip "Upload Product"). You can click it to choose a file or drag an image onto it. A product image is required. 4. Optional: add an avatar. Either upload your own image with the second round button (tooltip "Upload Avatar"), or click the avatar button (it shows "Select Avatar" at first) and pick a preset from "Avatar Presets". Hover over a preset and click the magnifier ("Enlarge preview") to see it larger, then click "Select Avatar". 5. Optional: add up to six reference images with the third round button (tooltip "Upload References"); you can select several files at once. They appear as small round thumbnails above the text box; hover over one and click its x to remove it. 6. Optional: instead of uploading, click "Saved" to reuse images you uploaded or generated before. The first pick fills the product slot, the next the avatar slot, then the references. 7. Click the format button (it shows "UGC" at first) and choose a preset from "Video Format Presets": UGC, Tutorial, Unboxing, Hyper Motion, Product Review or TV Spot. 8. Choose the aspect ratio (9:16 at first, "Aspect Ratio" list), the resolution (1080p at first, "Resolution" list: 720p or 1080p) and the duration (5s at first, "Duration" list: 4s to 15s). 9. Click "Launch". The button shows "Generating..." while the ad is made. 10. When it is ready the video opens full screen; click outside it or the close button to return to the page. The ad is also added at the top of the gallery, where hover shows the actions: copy prompt, "Download", Post to social, an AI assist star and "Delete".
studios.modelCapabilities: Marketing Studio has no model picker. The resolution you choose decides which backend is used (1080p or 720p); both take your script, up to eight images and a preset video.

studios.name: Body Swap
studios.description: Replaces the character in a video with a character from an image: you upload a source video and a character image, and the result is the new character performing the video's motion.
keyFeatures: Two required uploads: "Video" (source video) and "Character image"
Model dropdown with three models: Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control, Runway Act Two and Wan2.2 Animate
Optional text box ("Optional — describe the motion or scene..."), used only by models that accept a prompt
Aspect ratio list shown only for Runway Act Two; Orientation list shown only for Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control
"Library" (this browser's videos, images and results) and "Saved" (your saved uploads and generations from all studios)
Gallery with hover preview, full screen, copy prompt, Download, Post to social and Delete
studios.howToUse: 1. Open Body Swap at /studio/recast (the "Body Swap" tab in the studio tab bar). The controls are in the bar at the bottom of the page. 2. Add the source video, the clip whose movement you want to keep: click the first round button (tooltip "Upload video file, or drag and drop"), choose a file, or drag a video onto it. Videos must be under 50MB. 3. Add the character image, the person or character who should appear instead: click the second round button (tooltip "Upload character image file, or drag and drop") or drag an image onto it. Images must be under 10MB. 4. To remove an upload, click its round button again (the file name shows with "click to clear" in the tooltip). 5. Click the model button (it shows the current model name) and choose from the "Model" list: Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control (selected at first), Runway Act Two or Wan2.2 Animate. 6. If you chose Runway Act Two, an aspect ratio button appears; click it and pick a value from the "Aspect Ratio" list. If you chose Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control, an "Orientation:" button appears; choose "Image" or "Video" from the "Orientation" list (see the tips below). 7. Optional: type a note in the text box (placeholder "Optional — describe the motion or scene..."). It is used only by Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control and Wan2.2 Animate; Runway Act Two ignores it. 8. Click "Swap Body". The button shows "Swapping..." while the video is made. 9. When it finishes, the new video appears at the top of the gallery. Hover over it to preview, click it for full screen, and use the icons that appear on hover to copy the prompt, download ("Download"), post to social or delete ("Delete").
studios.modelCapabilities: Three models are listed in the "Model" dropdown: Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control (transfers the motion from your video onto the character image), Runway Act Two (drives the character image with the performance from your video; has an aspect ratio choice and no note box) and Wan2.2 Animate (animates a character or replaces one in existing clips).
limitations: Both uploads are required
File size limits
Kling orientation and length
Library is per browser
Gallery length
troubleshooting: Popup says "Please upload a source video first.": Upload a video with the first round button or choose one from "Library"/"Saved".
Popup says "Please upload a character image first.": Upload an image with the second round button or choose one from "Library"/"Saved".
Upload is refused: Check the size: video under 50MB, image under 10MB.
Generation fails: Try a shorter clip or a different model.
I cannot find the Aspect Ratio or Orientation button: Aspect Ratio appears only for Runway Act Two; Orientation only for Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control.

howToSteps: Open Body Swap at /studio/recast (the "Body Swap" tab in the studio tab bar). The controls are in the bar at the bottom of the page.

Add the source video, the clip whose movement you want to keep: click the first round button (tooltip "Upload video file, or drag and drop"), choose a file, or drag a video onto it. Videos must be under 50MB.

Add the character image, the person or character who should appear instead: click the second round button (tooltip "Upload character image file, or drag and drop") or drag an image onto it. Images must be under 10MB.
To remove an upload, click its round button again (the file name shows with "click to clear" in the tooltip).
Click the model button (it shows the current model name) and choose from the "Model" list: Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control (selected at first), Runway Act Two or Wan2.2 Animate.

If you chose Runway Act Two, an aspect ratio button appears; click it and pick a value from the "Aspect Ratio" list. If you chose Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control, an "Orientation:" button appears; choose "Image" or "Video" from the "Orientation" list (see the tips below).
Optional: type a note in the text box (placeholder "Optional — describe the motion or scene..."). It is used only by Kling 3.0 Pro Motion Control and Wan2.2 Animate; Runway Act Two ignores it.
Click "Swap Body". The button shows "Swapping..." while the video is made.

When it finishes, the new video appears at the top of the gallery. Hover over it to preview, click it for full screen, and use the icons that appear on hover to copy the prompt, download ("Download"), post to social or delete ("Delete").

studios.name: Layers Studio
studios.shortDescription: Canvas editor with a right-hand tools panel: split an image into layers, upscale, color grade, remove the background, expand the image, and run quick AI edits (Edit text, Enhancer, Relight, Angles).
studios.fullDescription: Layers Studio shows your image on a canvas, a floating toolbar and prompt bar at the bottom, and a Tools panel on the right. The panel opens on Layer Decomposition; use the back arrow (Back to Tools) to see the tool list: Layer Decomposition, Upscale, Color Grading, Remove background, Expand & Outpaint, Edit text, Enhancer, Relight and Angles. Each tool has its own action button at the bottom of the panel (for example 'Separate layers', 'Upscale', 'Remove Background', 'Expand Image'); there is no single 'Process' button. The studio starts with a sample image already loaded, so you can try it before uploading your own.
keyFeatures: Layer Decomposition: split an image into separate PNG layers (Resolution 1K / 1.5K / 2K, Layers slider 2 to 16) and browse them in a Layer Carousel
Upscale with three models: Topaz (x1, x2, x4, x8), SeedVR2 (2k, 4k, 8k) and AI Upscaler
Color Grading with live preview: Color Correct, Soften Details, Bloom, Halation, Lens Instructions, Exposure, Film Grain, plus Download and Post to social
Remove background (AI Background Remover) and Expand Image (AI Image Extension)
Quick AI edits: Edit text, Enhancer, Relight, Angles
Canvas tools: Lasso edit, Regional edit, Marker pen, Eraser, Shapes, Pan, zoom
Saved button to reuse images you uploaded or generated in any studio
howToSteps: Open Layers Studio from the studio tab bar or go to /studio/layers. A sample image is already on the canvas.

To use your own image, click the thumbnail button on the left edge (hover shows CHANGE, tooltip 'Upload or Change Image'), or click the + button in the prompt bar (tooltip 'Add Image'), or drop an image on the canvas. Images must be image files up to 20MB. You can also click Saved on the left to reuse an earlier image.
In the Tools panel on the right, click the back arrow (tooltip 'Back to Tools') to see the list, then click the tool you want.

Layer Decomposition: choose Resolution (1K, 1.5K or 2K) and drag the Layers slider (2 to 16). Optionally type instructions in the prompt bar at the bottom ('Describe how to edit image or split layers...'). Then click the lime button at the bottom of the panel that reads 'Separate layers' (the star button in the prompt bar, tooltip 'Run Layer Decomposition', does the same).

Upscale: click the Model box and pick Topaz, SeedVR2 or AI Upscaler. For Topaz choose Upscale Factor x1, x2, x4 or x8; for SeedVR2 choose Resolution 2k, 4k or 8k; AI Upscaler has no extra options. Click the button that reads 'Upscale' followed by a number.
Remove background: open Remove background and click 'Remove Background 1.0'. Expand: open Expand & Outpaint and click 'Expand Image 0.03'.

Color Grading: open Color Grading and move the sliders in each section (Color Correct, Soften Details, Bloom, Halation, Lens Instructions, Exposure, Film Grain). Use a section's Reset button, the reset-all button (tooltip 'Reset All Color Grading'), Download to save the graded image, or Post to social.

Edit text / Enhancer / Relight / Angles: open the tool and click its button (Run Text Edit, Enhance Image, Apply Relight, Apply Perspective Angle). Edit text has its own box 'Enter text modification prompt...'.
Wait for the progress overlay ('Processing Image...') to finish. Upscale, Remove background, Expand and the quick edits replace the image on the canvas with the result.
For layers, use the Layer Carousel: arrows (Previous Layer / Next Layer), the eye button (Toggle Visibility), Solo Active / Stack Mode, 'Save' for one layer, or 'Download All' for every layer.
gettingStarted: Open the Layers tab (/studio/layers).
Click the sample image's thumbnail (left edge) to upload your own image, or keep the sample to try the tools.
Pick a tool in the right panel (use the back arrow to see the list).
Click the action button at the bottom of the panel.
Download the result (Download All for layers, Save for one layer, Download in Color Grading).
tips: Click the sample card at the top of Layer Decomposition (tooltip 'Click to load this layer decomposition example') to load a ready-made 5-layer example without spending credits on a run.

Use Lasso edit or Regional edit to mark an area, type a prompt in the floating bar ('Type your prompt here...') and press Enter; marked areas are also added as layer regions for the next decomposition (a 'Clear (N)' button removes them).
Run Remove background first, then Upscale: the result of each tool becomes the image for the next one.
Color Grading is applied on your device; download or post it from the Color Grading footer.
The buttons show a number (for example 'Upscale 1.0', 'Expand Image 0.03', 'Remove Background 1.0'): these are fixed labels in the screen.
bestPractices: Use a clear image with distinct subjects before decomposing; raise the Layers slider only if you need more separate elements.
Check the canvas result before running the next tool, because the canvas image is replaced.
Download layers before you load another image or sample; uploading a new image clears the layer list.
Keep source images under 20MB (PNG, JPEG, WEBP).

studios.name: Workflows
studios.description: Browse template, personal and community workflows, run a workflow from a simple Playground form, or edit it on a node canvas (Full Workflow).
studios.shortDescription: Open a workflow from Templates, My Workflows or Community, run it in the Playground, or build and edit it in the Full Workflow canvas.
studios.fullDescription: The Workflows page has a list view and a workflow view. The list shows cards under three tabs: Templates, My Workflows and Community, with a Create Workflow button. Clicking a card opens the workflow, where two tabs let you either run it with a form (Playground) or open the node canvas (Full Workflow). In the Playground the form fields come from the workflow's own inputs, and the Run Workflow button shows the outputs as images, videos or text. In the canvas you add nodes, connect them, and use Run All, Publish and Save Workflow.
keyFeatures: Three list tabs: Templates, My Workflows, Community
Create Workflow button that makes an 'Untitled Workflow' and opens the canvas
Rename and Delete for your own workflows from the card menu
Playground tab: form generated from the workflow's inputs, Run Workflow button, results grid
Full Workflow tab: node canvas with node menu, Run All, Publish / Unpublish, Save Workflow
Zen mode that hides the top bar (Enter Zen Mode / Exit Zen)
Duplicate button when a workflow is not yours to edit
studios.howToUse: Open Workflows, pick a tab, click a workflow card (or Create Workflow). In Playground fill the Configuration fields and click Run Workflow; in Full Workflow edit the canvas and click Run All.
howToSteps: Open the Workflows tab (route /studio/workflows). You see the title 'Workflows' and the tabs Templates, My Workflows and Community.

Click a tab: Templates for ready-made workflows, My Workflows for ones you created, Community for workflows others published. Each workflow is a card with a category and name. If a tab is empty you see 'No workflows found in this section.'
Click a card to open it. The top bar shows All Workflows (back), the tabs Playground and Full Workflow, and the workflow name. Playground is the first view.
In Playground, fill the fields under Configuration. Each field is named by the workflow's own input (text fields are boxes, choices are dropdowns); starting values or examples are filled in for you.
Click Run Workflow. The button shows 'Generating...' and the right side shows 'Running Pipeline'. When it finishes you see 'Workflow Results' with a COMPLETED badge.
Look at the result cards: images, videos (with controls) or text. Hover a card to reveal the output id and a link button that opens the file in a new tab.

To change the workflow itself, click Full Workflow. The canvas opens; use the + button on the left, or right-click the canvas, to add nodes (Input Models, Text (LLMs), Generate Image, Edit Image, Generate Video, Edit Video, Generate Audio, Api Node, Utilities). The search box says 'Search nodes or models'.
Connect nodes by dragging between their handles and set each node's fields. Click Run All at the top right to save and run the whole workflow (it shows the total cost in dollars when known).
Click the workflow name at the top to open 'Save Workflow', type a name in 'Enter Workflow Name' and click Save. Use Publish (or Unpublish) to share or withdraw it.
Click All Workflows to return to the list. To create a new one, click Create Workflow on the list page.
gettingStarted: Open Workflows from the studio tabs (route /studio/workflows).
Start on the Templates tab and click a card that looks close to what you need.
In Playground, fill in the Configuration fields.
Click Run Workflow and wait for 'Workflow Results'.
If you want to change the steps, click Full Workflow. For templates you do not own the canvas is locked and shows Duplicate, which makes your own copy.
Use Create Workflow when you want to start from a blank 'Untitled Workflow'.
tips: Try a Template in Playground first to see what inputs and outputs look like.
Use Rename (card menu on My Workflows) to give workflows clear names.
Playground text fields for image or video inputs are plain text boxes: paste a link rather than choosing a file.
If you use the top bar toggle Enter Zen Mode, the bar becomes a small floating pill with Play, Builder and Exit Zen.
Run All saves the workflow before running it, so you do not need to save first.
bestPractices: Name each workflow clearly with Rename or Save Workflow before sharing it.
Test in Playground before publishing.
Duplicate a template instead of trying to edit it directly: a workflow you do not own cannot be edited.
Check the cost shown next to Run All before running big workflows.
Use Community to learn how other people connect nodes.

studios.shortDescription: Browse agent cards under Templates, My Agents and My Chats, and open one to chat; use Create to make your own agent.
studios.fullDescription: The Agents studio is a list page with a header called Agents, three tabs (Templates, My Agents, My Chats) and a Create button. Template and My Agents tabs show agent cards (picture or placeholder, category, name and, for community agents, 'By <owner>'). My Chats shows one card per past conversation with the agent name, chat title, how long ago it was updated and a message count. The agents themselves are hosted by MuAPI. Clicking an agent card opens that agent's own full-screen chat page (address /agents/<agent id>), which has a 'Back to Studio' link in the top-left corner. Create opens the agent creation page (/agents/create).

studios.howToUse: Open Agents, choose Templates, My Agents or My Chats, click a card to open the chat, type a message and send it. Use Create to build a new agent.
howToSteps: Open the Agents tab (route /studio/agents). The header says Agents and shows the tabs Templates, My Agents and My Chats.
Click Templates to see ready-made agents. Each card shows a category label (or 'AI Assistant' when none is set), the agent name and, for community agents, 'By <owner>'.
Click a card to open that agent. The agent's chat page opens full screen; use 'Back to Studio' at the top-left to return.

Type your message in the chat box and send it. In the chat view built into this studio the box says 'Message this agent...'; press Enter to send or Shift+Enter for a new line, or click Send. Agent replies are shown as formatted text.
Wait for the reply (a spinner shows while the agent works; the studio waits up to about 5 minutes before showing 'Agent response timed out.').
To continue an old conversation, click My Chats and click a conversation card; it opens the agent with that chat's history.
To see agents you made, click My Agents.

To make an agent, click Create (the + Create button at the top right). The create page opens. In the create form built into this studio the fields are Name, Description, System Prompt and 'Welcome Message (optional)', and the submit button is Create Agent.
gettingStarted: Open Agents from the studio tabs (route /studio/agents).
Stay on Templates and click an agent card that matches your task.
Type a message and send it.
Come back later through My Chats to continue the conversation.
Click Create when you want your own agent with your own System Prompt.
tips: Use My Chats to continue a conversation instead of starting over.
If a list fails to load click Retry.
A card that has no picture shows a placeholder icon; the agent still works.
The Welcome Message field is optional; when set it is shown at the start of an empty chat.
bestPractices: Try several template agents before creating your own.
When you create an agent, put the role and rules into System Prompt (placeholder 'You are a helpful assistant that...').
Give the agent a clear Name and short Description so you can find it in My Agents.
Keep messages specific; the agent only sees what you type in the chat.

studios.name: Design Agent AI
studios.description: A chat-based design assistant called Go-AI: describe what you want or pick a template, approve its plan, and get images, videos, audio or text assets back, with optional reference media and a Brand Kit.
studios.shortDescription: Chat with Go-AI, optionally pick a template and attach references, approve the plan, and download the generated assets.
studios.fullDescription: Design Agent AI opens on a home screen headed 'Design is easier with Go-AI'. A prompt box takes your request; beside it are a '+' button to upload reference media, a Templates pill, a reference counter (0/14 references) and a Send button. Under it, Recent Projects lists a New Project tile and your saved projects. Above the prompt are the mode pills (agent, generate, edit) and a Brand Kit button. Sending a message creates a project (if none is open) and starts a chat. Go-AI may first show an execution plan card with its steps and credit estimate; you press 'Approve & Generate' or 'Reject / Revise'. Results appear in the chat as asset thumbnails; click one to open a viewer with Download and image actions (Edit with Go-AI, Upscale, Remove BG, Vectorize, Enhance). The studio needs a paid SmartVideo GO plan; otherwise an upgrade prompt appears.
keyFeatures: Chat with Go-AI from a prompt box with typing placeholder suggestions
Templates picker with 30 built-in templates and a search box
Mode pills: agent, generate, edit
Brand Kit (logo, colors, fonts, tone, style) that is added to your messages when 'Use Brand Kit' is on
Upload reference media with '+' (up to 14 references per message, images, video or audio)
Execution plan card with 'Approve & Generate' and 'Reject / Revise'
Asset viewer with Download, Edit with Go-AI, Upscale, Remove BG, Vectorize, Enhance and a post-to-social button
Recent Projects with New Project tile and delete on hover
studios.howToUse: Open Design Agent AI, type what you want (or choose a template with Templates), optionally attach references and turn on Brand Kit, press Send, approve the plan if one appears, then click a result to download it or run an image action.
howToSteps: Open the Design Agent AI tab (route /studio/design-agent). Without a MuAPI key in place, sending, uploading or creating a project opens the API key window instead.
You land on the home screen 'Design is easier with Go-AI'. Optionally click one of the mode pills at the top (agent, generate, edit); agent is selected at first.
Optional: click the Brand Kit button, tick 'Use Brand Kit', fill the logo, colors, fonts, tone and style boxes, then click 'Save Brand Kit'. The Brand Kit button turns green while it is on.

Optional: click Templates, search with 'Search templates...' and click a template card. A chip showing the template id (for example logo-design) appears next to the Templates button; click its x ('Clear template') to remove it.

Optional: click the '+' button ('Upload reference media') and choose image, video or audio files. A counter shows how many of 14 references you used; 'Uploading reference…' appears while files upload, and each file shows as a chip you can remove.
Type your request in the prompt box (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a new line). You can also send with only a template or only attachments selected.
Click Send (the arrow button, 'Send message'). A project named 'Project 1', 'Project 2' and so on is created automatically if none is open, and 'Go-AI is planning' appears.

If a plan card titled 'GO-AI EXECUTION PLAN' appears, read its steps and the credit total, then click 'Approve & Generate' to run it, or 'Reject / Revise' to cancel it (the prompt box is pre-filled with 'Revise the plan: ' for you to explain what to change).
Wait while 'Go-AI is working...' is shown. Generated assets appear under Go-AI's reply.

Click an asset to open the viewer. Click Download to save it; for images you can also click Edit with Go-AI, Upscale, Remove BG, Vectorize or Enhance. Edit with Go-AI, Upscale, Remove BG and Vectorize switch to edit mode, attach the image and prefill the prompt; you then press Send.
Click '← Back' at the top-left of the chat to return to the home screen; your project is listed under Recent Projects.
gettingStarted: Open Design Agent AI from the studio tabs (route /studio/design-agent).
Make sure you are signed in. SmartVideo GO access is included with your account; if it is not active, sending shows an upgrade prompt.
Type a simple request such as the one suggested by the typing placeholder (for example 'Ask Go-AI to create a thumbnail...').
Press Send and wait for the plan or the result.
Click 'Approve & Generate' if a plan card shows.
Click a result and press Download.
tips: Use Templates to start from a ready-made recipe; you can still add your own text.
Turn on Brand Kit before generating so your colors, fonts, tone and style are sent with each message.
Attach reference images with the '+' button; they are listed in the chat with their labels.
After an image is generated, use Upscale, Remove BG or Vectorize from the viewer instead of retyping a prompt.
The placeholder text cycles through ideas such as 'Ask Go-AI to design a brand kit...' to show what you can ask.
bestPractices: Read the credit total on the plan card before pressing 'Approve & Generate'.
Use 'Reject / Revise' and explain changes rather than starting over.
Keep references to files that pass the upload check (see limits).
Download results you want to keep; chat messages are not restored when you reopen a project.
Fill all Brand Kit fields you care about; empty ones are sent as 'not set'.

faqs.question: Where do I open Design Agent AI?
faqs.answer: The Design Agent AI tab, route /studio/design-agent.

faqs.question: How many templates are there?
faqs.answer: The picker currently lists 30 templates (counted in DesignAgent.tsx) and has a search box.

faqs.question: What are the mode pills?
faqs.answer: agent, generate and edit; agent is selected first and the choice is sent with your message.

faqs.question: What is the Brand Kit?
faqs.answer: A dialog with logo, colors, fonts, tone and style boxes. When 'Use Brand Kit' is ticked these are sent with your messages.

faqs.question: How many references can I attach?
faqs.answer: Up to 14. The counter reads '<n>/14 references'.

faqs.question: What files can I attach?
faqs.answer: jpg/png/webp images up to 10 MB, mp4/webm/mov video up to 50 MB, mp3/wav/webm audio up to 10 MB.

faqs.question: What does Approve & Generate do?
faqs.answer: It approves Go-AI's execution plan so it starts generating; 'Reject / Revise' cancels it and prefills 'Revise the plan: '.

faqs.question: Are my projects saved?
faqs.answer: The list of projects and your Brand Kit are saved in this browser. Reopening a project shows an empty chat.

faqs.question: Can I edit generated images?
faqs.answer: Yes, open an image and use Edit with Go-AI, Upscale, Remove BG, Vectorize or Enhance.

faqs.question: Do I need to buy anything to use Design Agent?
faqs.answer: No extra purchase is needed: base SmartVideo GO access is included for every signed-in account. Sending and uploading check that access, and an upgrade prompt opens only if it is not active.

faqs.question: Generation is blocked, what do I check?
faqs.answer: Open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

studios.name: VFX Studio
studios.shortDescription: Turn one image into a short video with a chosen AI effect, camera move or VFX preset from a picture catalogue.
studios.fullDescription: The studio page is titled AI VFX Studio. You add one source image, pick an effect card from the catalogue (three categories: AI Effects, Motion Controls and VFX), optionally describe the subject in a text box, choose Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality, and click Generate. The result is a short video that you can download, copy as a URL, post to social, enhance or regenerate. The effect list is a fixed catalogue of named presets: the preset name decides the look and anything you type is added on top.
keyFeatures: Effect catalogue with three category tabs showing their counts (AI Effects, Motion Controls, VFX) and a Search effects box
Effect cards with preview pictures; click a card to select it
One source image: upload, drag and drop, or paste an image URL
Optional prompt to describe the subject
Aspect (9:16 Portrait, 16:9 Landscape, 1:1 Square), Duration (5s or 10s), Size (480p or 720p) and Quality (Medium or High)
Progress bar with Cancel while a video is generating
Result panel with Download, Copy URL, Post to social, Enhance, Regenerate and New Video
Your settings and last effect are remembered in this browser
Prompt and aspect ratio can arrive from a Storyboard hand-off or from a landing-page template
studios.howToUse: Open VFX Studio from the studio list (/studio/vfx-studio). Add an image with the Add image square (or paste an image URL), pick an effect card in one of the category tabs, optionally type a short description of the subject, choose the four settings, then click Generate ✨. When the video is ready use Download or the other buttons beside it.
howToSteps: Open VFX Studio from the studio list. The page shows the AI VFX Studio banner, an input panel and, below it, the effect cards.

Click the Add image square on the left of the input panel and choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP image (you can also drag a file onto the square). Alternatively paste an https:// link ending in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp into the …or paste an image URL (https://) and press Enter box and press Enter.
Wait until the image shows in the square. The Remove image button (an x on its corner) clears it if you picked the wrong one.
Choose a category tab: AI Effects, Motion Controls or VFX. Use Search effects... to find a card by name.
Click an effect card. The panel then shows Effect: followed by the card name.
Optional: type a short description in the box that starts with Optional: describe the subject (for example "a red sports car"). It is added on top of the effect.
Choose Aspect, Duration, Size and Quality in the row under the input.
Click Generate ✨. A window titled Generating your video... shows progress; you can click Cancel in the input panel to stop.
When the window says Your video is ready!, click Download to save the MP4, or Close to look at the result panel below the input.
In the result panel you can click Copy URL, Post to social, Enhance, Regenerate (run the same settings again) or New Video (clear everything and start over).
gettingStarted: Open VFX Studio from the studio list.
Add an image with Add image.
Click an effect card in the AI Effects tab, for example Fire.
Click Generate ✨ with the default settings (16:9 Landscape, 5s, 480p, Medium).
Download the finished video.
tips: Use a clear, well-lit image where the subject is easy to see; the effect is applied to that image.
Leave the prompt empty at first. The preset name already picks the look; add a prompt only to name the subject.
The default settings (16:9 Landscape, 5s, 480p, Medium) are the quickest way to test an effect; raise Size and Quality for the final version.
Choose 9:16 Portrait for vertical social videos.
Use Search effects... if you know the name; the search filters the cards of the category tab you are on.
bestPractices: Test an effect at the default size, then regenerate at 720p and High quality once you like it.
Match Aspect to where the video will be used before generating, because it cannot be changed afterwards without regenerating.
Keep the subject centered and uncluttered in the source image.
Use Regenerate to retry the same settings, and New Video when you want a different image or effect.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Generate shows 'Upload an image or paste an image URL first'
steps: Click Add image and choose a file, or paste an image URL and press Enter.
The link must start with http:// or https:// and end in .jpg, .jpeg, .png or .webp.
If the message says 'Invalid image URL', download the picture and upload it with Add image.
Use a JPEG, PNG or WebP image; the message says 'Please upload an image file' for other files.
If the message says the file is too large, reduce it below 10 MB.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Generation is blocked or does not start
steps: If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.
Check that your plan is active.
Read the Error message in the progress window and click Close.
Try again with Regenerate, or choose a different image or effect.
If you see 'Generation timed out. Please try again.' wait a little and retry.

commonProblems.howToFix: Use the prompt to name the subject, and choose a different card for a different look.

commonProblems.problem: The studio shows my last settings
commonProblems.whyItHappens: The studio remembers category, effect, prompt and options in this browser.
commonProblems.howToFix: Click New Video (after a result) or change the values by hand.

faqs.question: Where do I open VFX Studio?

faqs.answer: One image and one effect card. The prompt is optional.

studios.name: Thumbnail Studio
studios.description: Creates YouTube-style thumbnails from a text description. Pick a style, a category template chip, a model, a canvas size and a quality level, then generate 1 to 4 variations. Every prompt is automatically extended with click-through-rate (CTR) cues. Includes an Edit image mode with an optional mask, a Refine last result step, a personal gallery and a community gallery.
studios.shortDescription: Create YouTube-style thumbnails with automatic CTR cues, eight style buttons, ten template chips, size and quality presets, an Edit image mode, a personal gallery and a community gallery.
studios.fullDescription: Thumbnail Studio turns a short description into thumbnails for YouTube and other platforms. On the generate tab you write what the thumbnail should show (or click a template chip such as Gaming or Tutorial), choose one of eight styles, a model, a canvas size and a quality level, and click Generate. Behind the scenes the studio appends a block of click-through-rate cues to your text (strong focal point, high contrast, emotional expression, room for text and similar). You can ask for 1 to 4 variations at once, switch to Edit image mode to start from your own picture with an optional painted mask, and use Refine last result to change the newest image. Finished images land in the mine tab, which is stored in your browser, and can optionally be shared to the community tab.
keyFeatures: Describe your thumbnail in plain text, or start from one of ten template chips (Gaming, Tutorial, Finance, Fitness, Food, Tech, Reaction, Vlog, Music, Education)
CTR prompt engine: every generation appends click-through-rate cues (focal point, contrast, emotion, text-safe area) to your prompt
Eight style buttons: Cinematic, Vibrant, Bold Text, Face Focus, Minimal, Neon Glow, Retro, Photorealistic
Wand button 'AI enhance prompt' that rewrites your description before generating
MODEL / API dropdown with a 'Search models' box (GPT Image 2, GPT Image 1, DALL·E 3, DALL·E 2)
Six CANVAS SIZE presets and three QUALITY presets (Draft, Standard, Best)
Advanced options: output format (PNG, JPEG, WebP), compression slider, 1 to 4 variations, share-to-community switch
'✎ Edit image' mode with a reference image upload and an optional paint/erase mask
'Refine last result' step for follow-up changes to the newest image
Personal gallery (mine tab) kept in your browser and a community gallery (community tab)
Hand-off from GO-Viral and Storyboard that pre-fills the description
'Personalize' button below Generate and 'Post to social' / 'Enhance' buttons in the refine panel
studios.howToUse: Open /studio/thumbnail-studio, type a description (or click a template chip), pick a style, model, canvas size and quality, then click the Generate button at the bottom. Results appear in the mine tab.
howToSteps: Open Thumbnail Studio from the studio list (route /studio/thumbnail-studio). The Generate tab is open by default.

At the top, choose the mode: '✦ Generate' (text to thumbnail, the default) or '✎ Edit image' (start from a picture you upload). If you choose '✎ Edit image', add your picture in the REFERENCE IMAGE box ('Drop an image or click to upload'). Optionally click 'Add mask', then use 'Paint' and 'Erase' to mark the areas you want changed.

In the DESCRIBE YOUR THUMBNAIL box, type what the thumbnail should show, for example 'A dramatic gaming thumbnail with a shocked face and bold text...'. The Generate button stays disabled until this box has text.

Optional shortcut: click one of the template chips under the box (Gaming, Tutorial, Finance, Fitness, Food, Tech, Reaction, Vlog, Music, Education). A chip replaces the box content with a ready-made prompt that you can then edit.

Optional: click the wand button inside the box (tooltip 'AI enhance prompt'). An 'Enhanced:' line appears under the box and is used instead of your raw text when you generate. Editing the box text clears the enhanced version.
Under STYLE, click one of the eight styles: Cinematic (selected by default), Vibrant, Bold Text, Face Focus, Minimal, Neon Glow, Retro or Photorealistic.
Under MODEL / API, check the model shown (GPT Image 2 by default). Click it to open the list, type in 'Search models' if you want, and pick GPT Image 2, GPT Image 1, DALL·E 3 or DALL·E 2.
Under CANVAS SIZE, pick a size card (16:9 HD / YouTube HD is the first and the default). Under QUALITY, pick Draft, Standard (the default) or Best.

Optional: click 'Advanced options' to set OUTPUT FORMAT (PNG, JPEG or WebP; JPEG is the default), COMPRESSION (shown for JPEG and WebP only), VARIATIONS (1, 2, 3 or 4) and the 'Share to community' switch (on by default).
Click the large Generate button at the bottom. It reads 'Generate Thumbnail', or 'Generate 2 Thumbnails' (and so on) when VARIATIONS is above 1. A progress area shows the steps while MuAPI works.

When the images finish, the studio switches to the 'mine' tab (shown as Mine) and your new thumbnails appear first. Hover over an image to reveal icon buttons: 'Download', 'Reuse settings', 'Make private' / 'Make public' and 'Delete'. Click an image to enlarge it.
To tweak the newest result, go back to the generate tab, open 'Refine last result', type the change (for example 'Change the background to a dark cityscape...') and click 'Apply refinement'.
Use the 'community' tab to browse public thumbnails for ideas and click 'Reuse settings' on one to load its prompt back into the Generate tab.
gettingStarted: Open /studio/thumbnail-studio and stay on the generate tab.
Type a description in DESCRIBE YOUR THUMBNAIL, or click a template chip such as Gaming or Tutorial.
Pick a STYLE, a CANVAS SIZE and a QUALITY level.
Click the Generate button at the bottom.
Review the result in the 'mine' tab and use 'Download' to save it.
tips: Start with a template chip, then edit the pre-filled text to match your video; it is faster than writing from scratch.
Use VARIATIONS (under 'Advanced options') to get up to 4 versions in one click and compare them side by side.
Use Draft quality while exploring ideas and switch to Best for the version you will publish.
Pick the 16:9 HD or 16:9 size card for YouTube; 9:16 is labelled 'Shorts / TikTok' and 1:1 is labelled 'Instagram / square'.
Use the wand button 'AI enhance prompt' when your description is short; check the 'Enhanced:' text before generating.
Open the community tab for ideas and click 'Reuse settings' on any image to load its prompt and size back into the generate tab.
Turn off 'Share to community' before generating if you do not want the images to appear in the public gallery.
bestPractices: Describe one clear subject, an emotion and a background; the studio already adds contrast and focal-point cues for you.
Keep wording short and concrete; leave room in your description for the title text you will add later.
Generate several variations and compare them at small size before choosing one.
Download your favourites right away: the mine tab is stored only in this browser (up to 100 images) and is not a cloud backup.
Use 'Refine last result' for small changes to the newest image instead of rewriting the whole prompt.

inputDetails.name: Description text (DESCRIBE YOUR THUMBNAIL)
inputDetails.description: A three-line text box where you describe the thumbnail. The Generate button is disabled while it is empty.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Always
inputDetails.restrictions: Typing in the box clears any 'Enhanced:' version. No character limit is set in the studio code.

inputDetails.name: Template chip
inputDetails.description: Ten small buttons under the description box (Gaming, Tutorial, Finance, Fitness, Food, Tech, Reaction, Vlog, Music, Education). Clicking one replaces the box text with a ready-made prompt.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want a starting prompt for a video category
inputDetails.restrictions: Replaces what you typed; edit the text afterwards.

inputDetails.name: Style (STYLE)
inputDetails.description: Eight style buttons: Cinematic, Vibrant, Bold Text, Face Focus, Minimal, Neon Glow, Retro, Photorealistic. Cinematic is selected by default.
inputDetails.whenToUse: To label and steer the look of the thumbnail
inputDetails.restrictions: One style at a time.

inputDetails.name: Model (MODEL / API)
inputDetails.description: A dropdown with a 'Search models' box and four entries: GPT Image 2 (marked FEATURED, the default), GPT Image 1, DALL·E 3 and DALL·E 2.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want a different balance of quality, speed and cost
inputDetails.restrictions: Only the models in this list can be chosen here.

inputDetails.name: Canvas size (CANVAS SIZE)
inputDetails.description: Six size cards: 16:9 HD (YouTube HD), 16:9 (YouTube standard), 1:1 (Instagram / square), 9:16 (Shorts / TikTok), 4:3 (Classic format) and 2K (2K landscape).
inputDetails.whenToUse: To match the platform you will publish on
inputDetails.restrictions: The aspect ratio of the card is what is sent to the generator.

inputDetails.name: Quality (QUALITY)
inputDetails.description: Three cards: Draft (about 5s), Standard (about 15s, default) and Best (about 45s). The times are hints shown on the cards.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Draft for exploring, Best for final versions
inputDetails.restrictions: Times are approximate.

inputDetails.name: Output format
inputDetails.description: Under 'Advanced options': PNG (lossless), JPEG (smaller file, default) or WebP (best compression).
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you need a specific file type
inputDetails.restrictions: The COMPRESSION slider (10 to 100, default 85%) is hidden when PNG is selected.

inputDetails.name: Variations
inputDetails.description: Under 'Advanced options': buttons 1, 2, 3 and 4 set how many thumbnails are requested in one run.
inputDetails.whenToUse: For A/B testing several versions
inputDetails.restrictions: Maximum 4 per run.

inputDetails.name: Share to community switch
inputDetails.description: Under 'Advanced options': 'Share to community' with the hint 'Show in public gallery'. On by default.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Switch it off if the images should stay private
inputDetails.restrictions: You can also toggle individual images later with 'Make private' / 'Make public' in the mine tab.

inputDetails.name: Reference image (Edit image mode)
inputDetails.description: Shown after you click '✎ Edit image'. Drop or click to upload an image; it is uploaded to MuAPI when you generate.
inputDetails.whenToUse: When you want to change an existing picture instead of starting from text only
inputDetails.restrictions: Accepts image files. Without an uploaded image the studio still runs from your text alone.

inputDetails.name: Mask (optional, Edit image mode)
inputDetails.description: After uploading, click 'Add mask' to paint over regions with 'Paint' and remove strokes with 'Erase'; a brush-size slider and a reset button are shown. The help text reads 'Paint over the areas you want to change. The AI will edit only those regions.'
inputDetails.whenToUse: When only part of the picture should change
inputDetails.restrictions: Brush slider range is 5 to 80.

inputDetails.name: Refinement text (Refine last result)
inputDetails.description: A small text box inside 'Refine last result' with the placeholder 'Change the background to a dark cityscape...'. Click 'Apply refinement' to create one new image from your newest result.
inputDetails.whenToUse: For follow-up edits to the newest image
inputDetails.restrictions: Appears only after you have at least one image. It makes one image per click.

faqs.question: Where do I find Thumbnail Studio?
faqs.answer: Open /studio/thumbnail-studio, or pick Thumbnail Studio in the studio list.

faqs.question: What is the CTR prompt engine?
faqs.answer: It is an automatic step: every time you generate, the studio adds click-through-rate cues (single focal point, high contrast, emotional expression, room for text) to your description. There is no switch for it.

faqs.question: Which models can I use?
faqs.answer: The MODEL / API list offers GPT Image 2 (default), GPT Image 1, DALL·E 3 and DALL·E 2.

faqs.question: How many thumbnails can I create at once?
faqs.answer: Open 'Advanced options' and choose VARIATIONS 1, 2, 3 or 4.

faqs.question: What sizes are available?
faqs.answer: CANVAS SIZE offers 16:9 HD, 16:9, 1:1, 9:16, 4:3 and 2K. 16:9 HD is the default.

faqs.question: Where are my thumbnails saved?
faqs.answer: In the mine tab, stored in your browser (the newest 100 are kept). Use 'Download' to keep a copy.

faqs.question: Will my thumbnails be public?
faqs.answer: By default yes: 'Share to community' under 'Advanced options' is on, so new images are also saved to the public gallery. Switch it off before generating, or use 'Make private' on an image in the mine tab.

faqs.question: Can I edit a picture I already have?
faqs.answer: Yes. Click '✎ Edit image', upload it in the REFERENCE IMAGE box, optionally paint a mask with 'Add mask', then describe the result and generate.

faqs.question: How do I change just one part of my newest result?
faqs.answer: Open 'Refine last result', type the change and click 'Apply refinement'.

faqs.question: Can I post the thumbnail somewhere?
faqs.answer: After you have a result, a Personalize button appears below the Generate button, and the 'Refine last result' panel contains a 'Post to social' button and an 'Enhance' button.

faqs.question: Why does generating open an upgrade window?
faqs.answer: Generation is limited to accounts with SmartVideo GO access; without it the studio opens the upgrade window instead of generating.

studios.competitivePositioning: Purpose-built for thumbnails: size cards for common platforms, automatic CTR cues, template chips and a community gallery in one screen. For a wider model choice or general image work, use Image Studio.

glossary.CTR: Click-through rate: how often people click a video after seeing its thumbnail.
glossary.CTR prompt engine: The automatic step that appends click-through-rate cues to your description before generating.
glossary.STYLE: One of eight style buttons (Cinematic, Vibrant, Bold Text, Face Focus, Minimal, Neon Glow, Retro, Photorealistic).
glossary.Template chip: A small category button (Gaming, Tutorial, ...) that fills the description box with a ready-made prompt.
glossary.mine tab: Your own generated thumbnails, stored in this browser.

studios.name: AI Influencer Studio
studios.description: Builds an AI character portrait by clicking picture tiles for face, body and style options (plus an optional text line) and generating an image of it.
studios.shortDescription: Design an AI influencer or fantasy character by clicking picture tiles in a Builder panel, then generate and save the portrait.
studios.fullDescription: AI Influencer Studio is a point-and-click character designer. The Builder panel on the left has three tabs (Face, Body, Style) with groups such as Character Type, Gender, Ethnicity / Origin, Eye Color, Hair / Head Growth and Rendering Style. Every group shows picture tiles and always has one tile selected. A toolbar above the preview lets you pick an aspect ratio (3:4, 1:1, 9:16 or 16:9), click 'Shuffle' for a random combination and click 'Generate Character'. You can add an optional line of extra details in the text bar at the bottom. Results show in the centre preview and pile up in the 'Generated' column on the right, where you can re-open them, save them or send them on.
keyFeatures: Builder panel with three tabs: Face, Body, Style
Twenty picture-tile groups in total, each with one option always selected
'Shuffle' button for a random combination and 'Reset' to go back to the first option in every group
Aspect ratio buttons 3:4, 1:1, 9:16, 16:9
Optional extra-details text line
Selected-option pills with hover pictures and 'show more' / 'hide'
'Generated' history column on the right
'Save', 'Post to social', star and 'Personalize' buttons on the result
studios.howToUse: Choose one tile in each Builder group (or click Shuffle), pick an aspect ratio, optionally type extra details, then click 'Generate Character'. Click 'Save' to download the result.
howToSteps: Open AI Influencer Studio (route /studio/ai-influencer). The screen has three areas: the Builder panel on the left, the character preview with the toolbar in the centre, and a 'Generated' history column on the right.

In the Builder panel use the three tab buttons at the top: Face, Body and Style. Each tab lists groups of picture tiles. For example Face has Character Type, Gender, Ethnicity / Origin, Eye Color, Eye Type, Eye Features, Mouth & Teeth, Ears, Horns and Skin Conditions.

Click a tile in each group to choose it. One tile is always selected in every group (the first one by default) and the selected tile gets a check badge. There is no way to switch a group off, so look through every group on all three tabs, including Horns, Eye Features, Skin Conditions and Accessories & Markings, and pick the option closest to what you want.
To start over, click 'Reset' at the top of the Builder panel; it puts every group back to its first option. To try a random combination instead, click 'Shuffle' in the toolbar above the preview.
In the toolbar above the preview, choose the picture shape with the four buttons 3:4 (selected by default), 1:1, 9:16 and 16:9.

Optional: in the text bar at the bottom of the centre area, type extra details, for example 'neon cyberpunk lighting, dramatic shadows'. The placeholder reads 'Add extra details… e.g. neon cyberpunk lighting, dramatic shadows'. This text is added to the end of the prompt.

Check the small pills above the text bar: they list your current choices (the first 7, then 'show more' / 'hide'). Hover over a pill to see its picture; click a pill to jump to the Builder tab that contains it.
Click 'Generate Character'. The button shows 'Generating…' and the preview shows 'Generating your AI influencer…' while the image is made.
When the image is ready it appears in the preview with buttons in its lower-right corner: 'Save' (downloads a .webp file), 'Post to social', a star button and 'Personalize'.

Every result is also added to the 'Generated' column on the right (with a count such as '1 characters'). Click a thumbnail there to show it again in the preview. Hovering a thumbnail on a desktop screen reveals copy-prompt and copy-image buttons, a download button and the 'Post to social' and star buttons.
gettingStarted: Open /studio/ai-influencer.
Click through the Face, Body and Style tabs and choose one tile in each group (or click 'Shuffle').
Pick an aspect ratio (3:4, 1:1, 9:16 or 16:9).
Click 'Generate Character'.
Click 'Save' under the preview to download the image.
tips: Click 'Shuffle' a few times to find a starting look, then adjust single groups.

Remember a tile is always selected in every group; check groups such as Horns, Eye Features, Skin Conditions, Accessories & Markings and Hair / Head Growth, because their default options will be included in the prompt.
Use the pills above the text bar to review all current choices at once; click a pill to jump to its group.
Use the text bar for lighting, mood or background details that no tile covers.
Pick 9:16 for vertical profile images and 16:9 for wide banners.
Click 'Save' on results you like: the 'Generated' column is only kept while the studio is open.
bestPractices: Decide the character type, gender and rendering style first, then refine eyes, hair and details.
Keep the extra-details text short and visual.
Generate, review, then change one group at a time so you can see what changed.
Save each result you want to keep before reloading the page.

faqs.question: Where do I find AI Influencer Studio?
faqs.answer: Open /studio/ai-influencer or choose AI Influencer Studio in the studio list.

faqs.question: Which model does it use?
faqs.answer: nano-banana-pro. There is no model selector.

faqs.question: What are the three tabs in the Builder?
faqs.answer: Face, Body and Style. Each contains groups of picture tiles.

faqs.question: Can I turn an option off?
faqs.answer: No. Every group always has one tile selected and the first is the default. You can only change it to another tile.

faqs.question: What does Shuffle do?
faqs.answer: It selects a random tile in every group.

faqs.question: What does Reset do?
faqs.answer: It sets every group back to its first option.

faqs.question: Which aspect ratios are available?
Can I add my own text?
faqs.answer: Yes. Type extra details in the text bar at the bottom of the centre area; it is added at the end of the prompt.

faqs.question: How do I download the image?
faqs.answer: Click 'Save' in the lower-right corner of the preview, or the download button on a history thumbnail. The file is a .webp.

faqs.question: Are my previous images kept?
faqs.answer: They appear in the 'Generated' column while the studio is open; the column is not saved after a reload.

faqs.question: Can I upload a reference photo?
faqs.answer: There is no upload control in this studio.

studios.name: Social Publishing
studios.shortDescription: A four-step Publish to social window, opened from the studios, to write copy, make a thumbnail, choose connected accounts and publish an image or video.
studios.fullDescription: Social Publishing is not a studio tab of its own. It is a window (modal) titled Publish to social that opens on top of whatever studio you are in when you click a Post to social button next to a finished image or video. There is no /studio/social-publishing page: that old address now lands in Image Studio (/studio/image). The window has four steps shown at the top: Write, Thumbnail, Destinations and Review & Publish. It shows a Preview of the image or video on the right. Accounts are connected on the Destinations step (a Connect button opens the platform's authorisation page in a new tab), and the actual publish request is sent from that step with the Publish Now button. Video can go to YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and X; an image can go to Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and X.
keyFeatures: Opens as a window from Post to social buttons in the image and video studios (not a separate tab); the route is the studio you opened it from, for example /studio/image
Four steps: Write, Thumbnail, Destinations, Review & Publish
Write: AI helpers for post copy (Write Post, Improve, Tone, Length, Platform Optimize) with three copy variants and platform tabs (Master, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook)
Thumbnail: generate thumbnails from templates or a prompt, with Aspect Ratio, model, number of variations and Advanced options
Destinations: eight platforms, connect accounts, select one or more accounts, per-account settings (Privacy, Schedule, Tags, Location, Alt text for images)
Publish Now sends the post to every selected account, with per-account status and Retry for failures
Live Preview of the media beside the steps
studios.howToUse: Social Publishing is not a studio tab of its own. It is a window (modal) titled Publish to social that opens on top of whatever studio you are in when you click a Post to social button next to a finished image or video. There is no /studio/social-publishing page: that old address now lands in Image Studio (/studio/image). To use it: finish an image or video in a studio, click its Post to social button, move through Write and Thumbnail (both optional to browse), choose your accounts on Destinations, click Publish Now, and check the status list. Opened from Image Studio this is /studio/image; other studios open the same window from their own result buttons.
howToSteps: Make an image or video in a studio (for example Image Studio at /studio/image, Video Studio, VFX Studio, Storyboard or Motion Director).

Click the Post to social button next to the finished result (in Image Studio it is a small round button that appears when you hover a generated image on a wide screen; in VFX Studio it is a labelled button beside Download; in Motion Director it appears after you export the film). The Publish to social window opens with the first step, Write.

Write step: type what the post is about in Post topic (What is this post about?). Click Write Post to generate three copy variants, or use Improve, Tone, Length and Platform Optimize on the text. Use the tabs Master, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook to view copy per platform. Click Continue.
Thumbnail step (optional): choose Recommended or Explore Ideas, pick a template or type a prompt, set Aspect Ratio, and click Generate. You can click Continue without making a thumbnail.
Destinations step: click a platform tile (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads or X). Images show only the platforms that accept images.

Click the Connect button for that platform; the platform's authorisation page opens in a new tab. Approve access, return and click Refresh to list the account. You can also paste a known account ID under Add account manually (account ID) and click Add.
Tick the checkbox on each account you want to publish to. Click the arrow on an account card to open its settings (Privacy, Schedule, Tags, Location, and Alt text for images).
Check the Selected destinations box, then click Publish Now. Each account shows a status (queued, uploading, processing, published or failed) in Publish status; a failed one has a Retry button.
Click Continue to reach Review & Publish to see a summary of the media, thumbnail, copy and destinations, and the results. Close the window with Close or the X at the top right when you are done.
gettingStarted: Open a studio that makes images or videos, for example Image Studio at /studio/image.
Generate something, then click its Post to social button.
In the Publish to social window go to Destinations and connect an account with the Connect button for the platform.
Tick the account and click Publish Now.
Watch Publish status for published or failed.
tips: You can leave the window open while you authorise an account in the new tab; click Refresh afterwards to see it.
Choose the platforms first on Destinations; the platform tile shows a dot when an account of that platform is selected.
Press Esc or click outside the window to close it; your steps are kept for the current session of the page until you open it for another media item.
Use Retry on a failed destination instead of publishing everything again.
A video can go to every platform listed; an image only to the ones that accept images.
bestPractices: Check the Preview on the right to be sure the right media is selected before publishing.
Publish to one account first to make sure the connection works, then to several.
Keep copy platform-appropriate: the Write step warns when text is over a platform's length limit (YouTube 5000, Instagram 2200, TikTok 2200, Facebook 63206 characters) or has more than 30 hashtags.
Review the summary on the Review & Publish step before leaving the window.

studios.name: GO-Viral
studios.description: A browsable feed of AI image and video prompts collected from public X posts, with search, filters, a prompt detail window, and one-click sending of a prompt to another studio.
studios.shortDescription: Browse a feed of viral AI image and video prompts, copy them, or send them straight to another studio.
studios.fullDescription: GO-Viral shows a feed of AI image and video prompts discovered from public X (Twitter) posts. Each record keeps its original author, source link, preview and recommended model, and credits ImgLume as the curator. The studio has three views (Feed, Video Prompts, Academy), a left sidebar with search, sort, category, model, view and (for video prompts) availability and language filters, and cards that open a detail window with the full prompt. From a card or the detail window you can copy the prompt, open the original post, or send the prompt to another studio. GO-Viral is sold separately: accounts without it see a locked screen with an 'Unlock GO-Viral' button, and every other studio stays open. Browsing the feed itself does not use your MuAPI key.
keyFeatures: Feed view of image and video prompts with preview media
Video Prompts view with its own filters (Availability, Source Language)
Search box, 'Sort By' (Newest first / Oldest first), 'Categories' and 'Recommended Model' filters
Grid and list layouts with infinite scroll (30 per page)
'Prompt Details' window with full prompt, author, engagement, recommended model, categories and a 'Copy' button
Link back to the original post ('Open Source', 'View on X', 'Open on X')
'Open in Studio' / 'Create This Style' to send a prompt to Image Studio, Thumbnail Studio, AI Influencer Studio, Marketing Studio, Video Studio or Cinema Studio
'View details' demo page and 'Personalize This Demo' on each card
studios.howToUse: Open /studio/go-ai-viral, browse or search the Feed, click 'View Prompt' on a card, then use 'Copy Prompt' or 'Open in Studio'.
howToSteps: Open GO-Viral (route /studio/go-ai-viral). If your account has not unlocked it, you see a locked screen titled 'GO-Viral is sold separately' with an 'Unlock GO-Viral' button instead of the feed; every other studio stays open.
At the top of the studio, choose a view with the three buttons: 'Feed' (the default), 'Video Prompts' or 'Academy'. The header also shows how many prompts are in the feed (for example '120 prompts').

To find prompts, use the Search box in the left sidebar (placeholder 'Search prompts, tags...' in Feed, 'Search video prompts...' in Video Prompts). In the Feed view the list updates about half a second after you stop typing.

Narrow the list with the sidebar groups: 'Sort By' ('Newest first' or 'Oldest first'), 'Categories' (starting with 'All categories') and 'Recommended Model' (starting with 'All models'). In 'Video Prompts' view you also get 'Availability' ('With video + prompt', 'With video only', 'All prompts') and 'Source Language' ('All languages' or one language).
Under 'View' in the sidebar, switch between the grid (tooltip 'Grid view') and the list ('List view') layouts. Scroll down to load more; the list loads in pages of 30 and ends with '— End of feed —'.

On a card, click 'View Prompt' (or click the card itself) to open the 'Prompt Details' window. It shows the preview, the full prompt text, the original author, the recommended model, media type, categories and language.
In the 'Prompt Details' window click 'Copy' (or 'Copy Prompt') to copy the prompt text; the button briefly shows 'Copied!'. Click 'Open on X' or 'View on X' to see the original post.

To use the prompt in another studio, click 'Open in Studio' in the 'Prompt Details' window or 'Create This Style' on the card. A window titled 'Open in...' lists the studios you can send it to: for image prompts Image Studio, Thumbnail Studio, AI Influencer Studio and Marketing Studio; for video prompts Video Studio and Cinema Studio. Click one (or 'Cancel') and the studio opens with the prompt passed along.
Optional: click 'View details' in the top-right corner of a card to open that item's own demo page, or click 'Personalize This Demo' to open the personalization window for it.
In 'Video Prompts' view, the cards show a video preview. Click a card to open the 'Video Prompt' window with 'Open in Studio', 'View Details', 'Open Video' and 'Copy Prompt' buttons.
gettingStarted: Open /studio/go-ai-viral (unlock GO-Viral first if the locked screen appears).
Browse the Feed or switch to 'Video Prompts'.
Use the Search box and the sidebar groups to narrow the list.
Click 'View Prompt' on a card and use 'Copy Prompt'.
Or click 'Open in Studio', choose a studio in the 'Open in...' window and continue there.
tips: Use the Search box with a topic or a tag (the placeholder says 'Search prompts, tags...').
Use 'Recommended Model' to see prompts written for a particular model; the detail window shows the same value.
Switch to the list layout under 'View' to see more rows at once.
In 'Video Prompts' view leave 'With video + prompt' selected to see only items that have both a video and a prompt.
Check the 'Original Source' block in the detail window to credit the author when you reuse an idea.

After 'Open in Studio', check the receiving studio's settings: GO-Viral packages the prompt, title, an aspect ratio and a preview image reference, and each studio uses only what it supports (Thumbnail Studio and AI Influencer Studio, for example, use the prompt text, AI Influencer Studio also the aspect ratio).
bestPractices: Start broad with a category, then add a search term.
Read the full prompt in the detail window before sending it to a studio.
Keep the original source link when you share or publish work inspired by a prompt.
Pick the target studio that matches the media type: the 'Open in...' window offers image studios for image prompts and video studios for video prompts.
