studios.description: Generates a square product photo from a category and a style preset, optionally starting from a product image link and optionally saved under one of your brands.
studios.shortDescription: Pick a category and a style, optionally add a product image link, and generate a square product photo.
studios.fullDescription: Photo Studio makes product photography. You choose one of six categories (E-commerce, Lifestyle, Food & Beverage, Tech & Electronics, Beauty & Fashion, Health & Wellness), then one of five style buttons in that category, optionally paste a product image URL, and click 'Generate'. The studio creates one square (1:1) image, shows it under 'Result' and keeps a history per brand. The brand drop-down at the top right chooses which brand the result is saved under and which brand's history is shown. Photo Studio lives inside the Brand Studio frame, with the same left menu, and needs SmartVideo GO access to generate.
keyFeatures: Six category buttons with five style buttons each (30 styles in total, counted from the code)
Optional 'Product image URL (optional)' field
Brand drop-down starting on 'No brand'
'Generate' button with result polling (2-second checks, up to 90 tries)
'Result' panel with 'Download'
'History' grid for the selected brand
'Personalize' button when a photo exists
Shortcut from a brand's menu ('Photo Studio' link) with the brand pre-selected
studios.howToUse: Open /photo-studio, choose a category and a style, optionally paste a product image link, then click 'Generate'.
howToSteps: Open Photo Studio at /photo-studio (it opens inside the Brand Studio frame; you can also click 'Photo Studio' under 'Tools' in the left menu, or 'Photo Studio' under a brand). The page is titled 'Photo Studio' with the line 'Generate product photography with AI'.

Optional: use the drop-down at the top right (it starts on 'No brand') to pick one of your brands. Picking a brand attaches your result to that brand and shows that brand's earlier photos under 'History'.
Click a category button: E-commerce (selected by default), Lifestyle, Food & Beverage, Tech & Electronics, Beauty & Fashion or Health & Wellness. Each category shows its own five style buttons.
Click one style button. You must choose a style: the 'Generate' button stays disabled until you do, and changing the category clears your style.
Optional: paste the web address of your product photo into the box 'Product image URL (optional)'. It must be a link to an image that can be opened publicly.
Click 'Generate'. The button shows a spinner while the photo is made; the studio checks for the result every 2 seconds for up to about 3 minutes.
When it is ready, a 'Result' panel shows the photo. Click 'Download' to open the full image in a new browser tab, then save it from there.
Scroll to 'History' (shown when a brand is selected) to see earlier photos for that brand with their style and category.
Optional: click 'Personalize' next to the brand drop-down (it appears once there is a photo) to send the newest photo to the personalization window.
gettingStarted: Open /photo-studio.
Click a category such as E-commerce.
Click a style such as Studio White.
Optionally paste a product image link.
Click 'Generate' and then 'Download'.
tips: Choose the category first: the style buttons change with it.
Use a clear, well-lit product picture for the 'Product image URL (optional)' field and make sure the link opens the image directly.
Pick a brand in the drop-down if you want the photo saved under it and visible in 'History'.
Try several styles of the same product to compare looks.
The result is square (1:1), which suits product listings and social feeds.
bestPractices: Start without a product link to explore styles, then add your product image for the final shot.
Use one category per product type so the style buttons fit.
Download results straight away from the 'Result' panel.
Keep the product link public: private or login-protected links cannot be read.

studios.name: Brand Studio
studios.description: Paste a website address to create a brand profile (Brand DNA) you can edit, then generate four campaign concepts and platform-sized creatives for that brand. Photo Studio is available from the same menu.
studios.shortDescription: Create a brand profile from a website address, then generate campaign concepts and creatives for eight platforms.
studios.fullDescription: Brand Studio is a small workspace with one flow. On the 'New Brand' page you paste a website address and click 'Analyze'; the studio fetches the page and creates a brand entry (it reads the site's title or site name and its description to fill Brand Name and Tagline). On the Brand DNA page you edit and save the brand's identity, voice, colors, fonts and imagery style. From there you click 'New Campaign', choose a goal and click 'Generate 4 Concepts'. On the campaign page you pick a concept and one or more platforms (Instagram Feed, Instagram Story, LinkedIn, Facebook Ad, X / Twitter, Web Banner, Email Header, YouTube Thumbnail) and click 'Generate Selected Assets'; the results are shown under 'Generated Assets'. A left menu lists your brands and links to 'Photo Studio'. Creating brands needs SmartVideo GO access.
keyFeatures: 'New Brand' page: website address box and 'Analyze' button with three progress lines
Editable Brand DNA page: Core Identity, Voice & Personality, Colors, Fonts, Imagery Style, with 'Save'
Six campaign goals and an optional creative-direction box
'Generate 4 Concepts' creates four concept cards (title, tagline, visual theme)
Eight platform buttons for assets with progress per platform
'Generated Assets' cards with image, headline, body and call to action
Left menu with your brands, 'New Campaign' and 'Photo Studio' shortcuts
'Personalize' button on the Brand DNA page when the brand has a screenshot
studios.howToUse: Open /brand-studio, paste a website address and click 'Analyze', edit the Brand DNA and click 'Save', then click 'New Campaign', choose a goal, click 'Generate 4 Concepts', pick a concept and platforms and click 'Generate Selected Assets'.
howToSteps: Open Brand Studio at /brand-studio (choose 'Brand Studio' in the studio list). The page is titled 'New Brand'. A menu on the left (a row of buttons at the top on a phone) has 'New Brand', your 'Brands' and a 'Tools' group with 'Photo Studio'.
Click in the box that shows the placeholder 'https://your-brand.com' and type or paste the full web address of the brand's website.
Click 'Analyze'. Three progress lines appear in turn: 'Fetching website...', 'Analyzing brand identity...' and 'Saving brand DNA...'. When it finishes you land on the brand's Brand DNA page.

On the Brand DNA page, review and complete the details. 'Core Identity' has Brand Name, Industry, Tagline, Value Proposition and Target Audience. 'Voice & Personality' has Tone of Voice, Personality and Key Messages. 'Colors' has Primary and Secondary colors. Below are Fonts and Imagery Style.

To add an item to Tone of Voice, Personality, Key Messages or Fonts, type it in the 'Add...' box and press Enter or click the plus button; click the small x on an item to remove it. To add a color, pick one with the color box or type a six-digit hex value such as #1a2b3c, then click the plus button.
Click 'Save' (top right). The button shows 'Saved' for a moment when your changes are stored.

Click 'New Campaign' (top of the Brand DNA page, or under the brand in the left menu). Choose one goal card: Product Launch, Lead Generation, Brand Awareness, Engagement, Thought Leadership or Direct Sales. Optionally type extra guidance in the 'Optional creative direction...' box.
Click 'Generate 4 Concepts' (it stays disabled until you choose a goal). When it finishes you land on the campaign page.

On the campaign page, under 'Concepts', click the concept card you want (the first one is selected by default). Under 'Platforms', click one or more platform buttons: Instagram Feed, Instagram Story, LinkedIn, Facebook Ad, X / Twitter, Web Banner, Email Header, YouTube Thumbnail.

Click 'Generate Selected Assets' (it shows how many platforms are selected, for example 'Generate Selected Assets (3)'). Each platform shows 'Queued...', then 'Generating...' and finally 'Done' or a 'Failed:' message; two platforms are worked on at a time.
When the run ends, your results appear under 'Generated Assets' as cards with the image, the platform name, a headline, body text and a call to action.
To make product photos for the brand, click 'Photo Studio' under the brand in the left menu or at the top of the Brand DNA page; the brand is pre-selected there (see the Photo Studio guide).
gettingStarted: Open /brand-studio.
Paste your website address into the box ('https://your-brand.com') and click 'Analyze'.
On the Brand DNA page, fill in the details and click 'Save'.
Click 'New Campaign', choose a goal and click 'Generate 4 Concepts'.
Pick a concept and platforms, then click 'Generate Selected Assets'.
tips: Use the full address including https://.
After 'Analyze', fill in the empty Brand DNA fields (Industry, Value Proposition, Colors and so on) and click 'Save': the campaign steps use the brand details you provide.
Colors must be written as six-digit hex values such as #1a2b3c.
Give a creative direction in the optional box when you have a specific angle in mind.
Select only the platforms you need; each selected platform is a separate generation.
Use the brand list in the left menu to jump back to an earlier brand.
bestPractices: Review and save the Brand DNA before creating a campaign.
Choose a goal that matches the real objective (for example Lead Generation vs Brand Awareness).
Start with one or two platforms to check the look before generating all eight.
Use a publicly reachable website address.

studios.name: Motion Director
studios.shortDescription: Chat with an AI director that plans a storyboard for a product film (using your website's real pages if you give a link), builds it from motion shot cards, and lets you render an MP4 or keep editing in the Motion Workbench.
studios.fullDescription: Motion Director opens on a chat page. You describe the film you want (a message with a site address makes the film use real pages from that site), choose an aspect ratio, optionally attach images, videos or audio, optionally pick shot cards from Templates, and click Generate. The director then asks how to proceed (use the Ink Press template, let the director pick shots, choose shot cards, or work it out together step by step), writes a storyboard for you to read, and builds the film only after you click Approve & build film. The finished film plays in the chat with buttons to render an MP4, render a fast draft, render without music, or open the film in the Motion Workbench, an editor with a timeline, an inspector, a library of shots, sounds and themes, and an Edit agent chat. Work is kept in this browser; a film or project saved earlier in the old Motion Studio shows up here too.
keyFeatures: Chat-driven film director: describe the film, answer the director, approve the storyboard
Option to Work it out together: a product check, three visual directions and a feature-to-shot map, each confirmed in chat
Decisions (visual direction, feature-to-shot map) are written into the chat before the storyboard
Storyboard card with Approve & build film and Revise
Real site pages: put a link in your message; a quick capture happens before the storyboard and more pages are captured when the film is built
Templates picker of shot cards with categories and search (up to 12 chosen cards per film)
Brand Kit button for business name, colours and logos
Attach images, videos and audio to the film
Seven-step progress strip: Product, Capture, Storyboard, Animate, Beat sync, Frame QA, Deliver
Final film player with Render MP4, Fast draft, Render without music, Download MP4 and Design spec
Motion Workbench editor: Media, Motion, Sound and Themes library tabs, timeline, inspector, Edit agent, Export video
Continue editing tile and Recent Projects; films from the removed Motion Studio reopen here
Leave confirmations while an MP4 is rendering and a browser prompt while files upload
studios.howToUse: Open Motion Director from the studio list (/studio/motion-director); the chat page opens. Type what film you want (include your site link to use its real pages), choose the aspect ratio, optionally attach files or pick shot cards in Templates, and click Generate. Answer the director's question, read the storyboard, click Approve & build film, then render the MP4 or open the film in the Motion Workbench.
howToSteps: Open Motion Director from the studio list. You see the heading Films are easier with Motion Director and a message box.

Optional: click Brand Kit to add your business name, colours and logos (it turns into Brand Kit · On once a brand is selected). Optional: click the + button (Attach image / video / audio) to add pictures, videos or music.

Type your request in the box, for example Create a 30-second promotional film from my website... (put your site address in the message to use its real pages, and say the length you want in the message, like 30 seconds; if you do not say, 20 seconds is used). Choose the aspect ratio with the 16:9 button (the menu offers 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1).

Optional: click Templates, search with Search recipes..., open a category chip, and click a shot card to add it. You can pick several; they appear as chips next to Templates and the film uses them in order.

Click the send button, which is labelled Generate for a new film. If you gave no template or shot names, the director replies with a question: click Use Ink Press, Let the director pick shots, Choose shot cards…, or Work it out together.

If you chose Work it out together, the director first runs a Product check and asks you to confirm. Click Looks right — next (or answer in your own words), then pick a visual direction with Use A, Use B or Use C (or Use my recommendation), then check the feature-to-shot map and click Looks right — write the storyboard. You can click You decide at any step to let the director choose the rest.
Wait while the progress strip runs. A button ■ Stop cancels storyboarding or building at any time.
Read the storyboard card (scenes, lengths, and whether it uses your site). To change it, type what to change in the message box or click Revise; to accept it, click Approve & build film.

When the film is ready, a FINAL FILM card appears with a player. Click Render MP4 to make the file (the page must stay open), or Fast draft for a smaller quicker version, or Render without music if the film has a music track. When rendering finishes click Download MP4.
To edit shots, copy, timing and sound, click Open in Motion Workbench. Use Back to chat to return; the film stays under Continue editing.
To start another film, click ↺ New film or type a new request.
gettingStarted: Open Motion Director from the studio list.
Write what film you want and include your site link if you have one.
Click Generate and choose Use Ink Press when asked (the quickest path).
Read the storyboard and click Approve & build film.
Click Render MP4 and then Download MP4.
tips: Put your site address in the message: the film then shows your real pages and logo. Without one the director uses sample pages.
Say the length in your message (for example 30 seconds). Films are planned between 5 and 90 seconds and 2 to 14 scenes.
Use the Templates picker to force specific shot cards; up to 12 can be chosen.
Reply to the director in plain words: say looks right, you decide, or name what to change.
Use Fast draft while experimenting; render the full size at the end.
Keep the tab open while an MP4 renders; closing or reloading cancels it.
bestPractices: Give the director a clear product name and a link; answer the product check honestly because later steps use it.
Review the storyboard card before approving; revising is cheaper than rebuilding the film.
Attach your own music if you want cuts on its beat; the progress strip says when no music is attached.
After building, open the Motion Workbench for fine edits instead of starting a new film.
Render the MP4 on a computer with enough memory; very long or heavy films take longer (the card shows a rough minutes estimate).

limitationDetails.limitation: The director needs your OpenAI key
limitationDetails.impact: Without it planning steps fail with a message asking you to add the key; Work it out together falls back to the Ink Press template.
limitationDetails.workaround: Open the Settings and add your OpenAI key.

limitationDetails.impact: Without active SmartVideo GO access, clicking Generate shows the upgrade prompt.
limitationDetails.workaround: Check your plan.

limitationDetails.limitation: MP4 renders in your browser tab
limitationDetails.impact: Closing or reloading the tab cancels the render, and leaving the page shows a confirmation.
limitationDetails.workaround: Keep the tab open; use Fast draft for quicker tests.

limitationDetails.limitation: Films are 5 to 90 seconds with 2 to 14 scenes
limitationDetails.impact: Plans outside these limits are adjusted.
limitationDetails.workaround: Split a longer story into several films.

limitationDetails.limitation: At most 12 chosen shot cards per film

limitationDetails.limitation: Projects are saved in this browser

troubleshootingSteps.issue: Nothing happens when I click Generate
steps: Make sure there is text in the box (or a picked shot card).
If an upgrade prompt appears, sign in again; if it persists, contact support so your access can be checked.
Wait if the strip shows Storyboarding… or Building the film…; press ■ Stop first to send a new request.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: The director says it needs an OpenAI key
steps: Open the Settings, add your OpenAI key, then send your request again.
Or click Use Ink Press, which can run without the guided steps.
The film continues with sample pages. Check that the link is a public site.
Send the address again, or attach screenshots with the + button, and the director re-captures.

troubleshootingSteps.issue: MP4 render fails or says the browser cannot encode MP4
steps: Use a current Chrome or Edge on a computer.
Try Fast draft.
Click the retry button (Render failed — retry) to try again.
It appears when an MP4 is still rendering: 'An MP4 is still rendering. Leaving cancels it. Leave anyway?'. Click Cancel to stay and let it finish.
The browser also asks before you close or reload the tab while a render or an upload is running.
Scroll to Recent Projects and click Continue editing or the film's tile.
Use the same browser you used before.
If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your keys.

faqs.question: Where do I open Motion Director?
faqs.answer: From the studio list at /studio/motion-director. The tab always opens the chat page; the editor opens at /studio/motion-director/workbench.

faqs.question: What is the button to start building?
faqs.answer: After the storyboard appears, click Approve & build film. The first message is sent with the send button labelled Generate.

faqs.question: Do I need a website?
faqs.answer: No. Without a link the film uses sample pages; a link or attached screenshots make it use your real pages.

faqs.question: How do I set the length?
faqs.answer: Say it in the message (for example 30 seconds). The default is 20 seconds.

faqs.question: What does Work it out together do?
faqs.answer: It runs a Product check, proposes visual directions and a feature-to-shot map, and waits for your confirmation at each step before writing the storyboard.

faqs.question: How do I change the storyboard?
faqs.answer: Type what to change in the box or click Revise.

faqs.question: How do I get an MP4?
faqs.answer: Click Render MP4 on the FINAL FILM card (or Export video in the Workbench), wait, then click Download MP4.

faqs.question: What happens if I leave while rendering?
faqs.answer: The render is cancelled; the studio asks you to confirm first.

faqs.question: Where is Continue editing?
faqs.answer: Under Recent Projects. It also shows a project recovered from the old Motion Studio.

faqs.question: Can I use my own music?
faqs.answer: Yes. Attach an audio file with the + button before generating.

faqs.question: How many shots can I choose?
faqs.answer: Up to 12 shot cards per film.

faqs.question: Can I publish the film?
faqs.answer: After an export in the Workbench, click Post to social.

studios.shortDescription: Browse the SmartVideo GO AI app collection, try live demos, open deployment guides and source code, and compare the reseller packages.
studios.fullDescription: SmartVideo GO AI Apps is the reseller marketplace page (route /studio/apps). Its top section introduces the reseller program and links to the Reseller Deployment Center. Under 'Choose How You Build' it shows two packages: 'DIY App Builder' ($197 one-time) and 'Apps + Training' ($597 one-time), each with a button that opens Stripe Checkout in a new tab, plus an upgrade button for the $400 difference. 'How It Works' explains the three steps (Choose Your App, Customize & Build, Launch Your Business) and links to the 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough'. Below that, 'The Application Collection' lists app cards you can search and filter by category. Each card can offer 'Try Live Demo', 'Deployment Guide', 'Source Code', 'Deploy on Vercel' and 'Learn How to Launch This App'. This studio does not generate media; it is a catalogue and a route to deployment and training.
keyFeatures: Searchable and filterable catalogue of apps (categories: Image, Video, Business, Productivity, Audio, Creative, Real Estate, Design, Lifestyle, Marketing)
'Try Live Demo' opens a working demo in a new tab
'Deployment Guide' links to the app's section in the Reseller Deployment Center
'Source Code' opens the app's GitHub repository
'Deploy on Vercel' starts a Vercel import for apps that are deployable templates

studios.howToUse: Open /studio/apps, search or filter for an app, then use the buttons on its card: 'Try Live Demo', 'Deployment Guide', 'Source Code', 'Deploy on Vercel' or 'Learn How to Launch This App'. Use 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough' for the full guided course.
howToSteps: Open SmartVideo GO AI Apps at /studio/apps (choose 'SmartVideo GO AI Apps' in the studio list). The top of the page shows the 'SMARTVIDEO AI APPS RESELLER PROGRAM' banner with the headline 'Your Apps. Your Brand. Your Business.'. The button 'Open the Reseller Deployment Center' opens the full deployment documentation at /reseller/deployment.

Read the two package cards under 'Choose How You Build': 'DIY App Builder' ($197, one-time, button 'Get All Apps') and 'Apps + Training' ($597, one-time, marked 'Most complete', button 'Get All Apps + Training'). A package button opens Stripe Checkout in a new tab; the page notes that your purchase is verified server-side before access is granted.

If you already own 'DIY App Builder' and want the training, click 'Upgrade to Apps + Training for $400' under the cards. The studio then shows 'Redirecting to secure checkout…'. If you already have the training it says 'You already have the Apps + Training package, so there is nothing to upgrade.'; if the upgrade does not apply to your account it explains that it is only for owners of the DIY App Builder package.

Scroll to 'How It Works' for the three steps: 'Choose Your App', 'Customize & Build' and 'Launch Your Business'. Under them, click 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough' to open the guided course at /academy/reseller/launch. The course page asks you to sign in and is available to accounts with the Apps + Training package; other accounts see a locked panel.

To browse the collection, go to 'The Application Collection'. Type in the box 'Search SmartVideo GO AI Apps...' to search app names, descriptions and categories (the list updates after a short pause), and click a category button to filter: All, Image, Video, Business, Productivity, Audio, Creative, Real Estate, Design, Lifestyle or Marketing. A line such as 'Showing 12 of 38 applications' shows how many apps match. If nothing matches you see 'No apps found matching your criteria.'.

Look at an app card: it shows a preview picture, the category, the name and a short description. Click the preview picture (or 'Try Live Demo') to open the working demo in a new tab. Cards without a hosted demo have no 'Try Live Demo' button.
Click 'Deployment Guide' on a card to open that app's instructions in the Reseller Deployment Center (/reseller/deployment, jumping to the app's section).

Click 'Source Code' to open the app's GitHub repository in a new tab. If an app has no published repository the button is greyed out and its tooltip reads 'Repository not yet published'. A small 'GitHub' link at the bottom of the card goes to the same repository.

Click 'Deploy on Vercel' to start importing the app's repository into your own Vercel account in a new tab. Only apps that are published as deployable templates have this button active; on the others it is greyed out and the tooltip reads 'Deploy unavailable — this app's source repository is not published as a deployable template.'

Click 'Learn How to Launch This App' to open that app's guided launch workshop in the Reseller Academy (/academy/reseller/apps/<app id>). Like the walkthrough, it needs you to be signed in and to have the training access.
For a complete beginner-to-launch route, follow 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough' (/academy/reseller/launch) alongside the 'Deployment Guide' of the app you picked.
gettingStarted: Open /studio/apps.
Search or pick a category to find an app.
Click 'Try Live Demo' to see it working.
Click 'Deployment Guide' for the setup instructions and 'Source Code' for the repository.
Click 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough' for the guided course.
tips: Use the category buttons first, then the search box, to narrow a long list.
Open 'Try Live Demo' before anything else to see what an app does.
Read the app's 'Deployment Guide' before you click 'Deploy on Vercel'.
If 'Deploy on Vercel' is greyed out, use 'Source Code' and the 'Deployment Guide' instead.
The 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough' course is the guided route from choosing an app to launch.
The 'GitHub' link at the bottom of a card and 'Source Code' go to the same repository.
bestPractices: Pick one app first and follow its guide to the end before adding more.
Check the package cards to decide between self-guided ('DIY App Builder') and guided ('Apps + Training').
Sign in with the same account you used to buy, so access to the walkthrough and workshops can be recognised.
Use the Reseller Deployment Center for the full setup steps.

faqs.question: What is SmartVideo GO AI Apps?
faqs.answer: The reseller marketplace page at /studio/apps: a catalogue of ready-made AI apps with demos, deployment guides, source code links and launch workshops, plus the two reseller packages.

faqs.question: What do the two packages cost?
faqs.answer: 'DIY App Builder' is $197 one-time and 'Apps + Training' is $597 one-time. Upgrading from DIY to training is a $400 difference.

faqs.question: What does 'Try Live Demo' do?
faqs.answer: It opens the app's hosted demo in a new tab. Cards without a hosted demo have no such button.

faqs.question: What does 'Deployment Guide' do?
faqs.answer: It opens the Reseller Deployment Center at /reseller/deployment, at the section for that app.

faqs.question: What does 'Source Code' do?
faqs.answer: It opens the app's GitHub repository in a new tab. It is greyed out when no repository is published.

faqs.question: Why is 'Deploy on Vercel' greyed out?
faqs.answer: It is active only for apps whose repository is published as a deployable template. For the others the tooltip says 'Deploy unavailable — this app's source repository is not published as a deployable template.'

faqs.question: What is 'Learn How to Launch This App'?
faqs.answer: A link to that app's guided workshop in the Reseller Academy (/academy/reseller/apps/<app id>). It needs sign-in and training access.

faqs.question: Where is the Reseller Setup Walkthrough?
faqs.answer: Click 'Reseller Setup Walkthrough' under 'How It Works', or go to /academy/reseller/launch. You must be signed in; accounts without the Apps + Training package see a locked panel.

faqs.question: How do I filter the apps?
faqs.answer: Use the category buttons (All, Image, Video, Business, Productivity, Audio, Creative, Real Estate, Design, Lifestyle, Marketing) and the 'Search SmartVideo GO AI Apps...' box.

faqs.question: Does this studio generate images or video?
faqs.answer: No. It is a catalogue and entry point to the apps, guides and training.

faqs.question: How does payment work?
faqs.answer: The package buttons open Stripe Checkout in a new tab. Your purchase is verified server-side before access is granted.

studios.name: Edit Studio
studios.shortDescription: A gallery of 14 one-purpose AI tool cards (image and video generators, upscaler, background remover, watermark remover, face swap, product shot, lip sync, editors, motion controls, audio, anime). Each card opens its own playground.
studios.fullDescription: Edit Studio opens on a gallery of tool cards titled "AI tools, one click away". Each card is a standalone tool: click it to open a playground at /studio/edit/<tool-name> with only the upload boxes, prompt box and settings that the selected model needs. You can filter the gallery by All, Image, Video or Audio, switch tools from a dropdown without going back, run several generations in one session, download each result and send a result back in as the next input. Which upload boxes and settings appear depends on the model you pick in the Model dropdown.
keyFeatures: Gallery of 14 tool cards (counted from the EDIT_TOOLS list in editTools.js), filterable by All, Image, Video and Audio
Each tool has its own shareable address: /studio/edit/<tool-name>
Playground built from the chosen model: upload boxes, Prompt box and a Settings panel change with the model
Upload a file, paste a file URL, or pick a saved file with the Saved button
Result panel with Download and Use as input, plus a This session strip to flip between earlier runs
Switch tool dropdown to jump to another tool without returning to the gallery
howToSteps: Open the Edit tab in the studio tab bar, or go to /studio/edit. You will see the gallery headed "AI tools, one click away".
Optionally click All, Image, Video or Audio above the cards to show only that kind of tool.
Click the card for the tool you want (for example Background Remover). Each card shows its name, a one-line hint and the number of models it offers.
In the playground, if the Model dropdown is shown, choose a model. Each model has its own upload boxes and settings.

Add the required inputs. Boxes marked with an asterisk (*) are required; boxes marked (optional) can be skipped. For each box, click it or drop a file on it, or paste a link under "or paste an image URL" (the word changes to video or audio for those boxes) and click Add, or click Saved to pick a file you uploaded or generated earlier.
If a Prompt box is shown, type what you want. A Prompt marked with * is required; the placeholder text tells you what to write.
If a Settings panel is shown, adjust the options. Changing the model resets Settings to that model's defaults.
Click Generate. While it runs, the Result panel shows "Generating…" with a seconds counter and the button reads Run again.
When the result appears, click Download to save it, or Use as input to send it into the first matching upload box of the same tool for another pass.
To compare runs, use the This session strip (it appears after the second run) and click a thumbnail. Use ← All tools to go back to the gallery, or Switch tool to open a different one.
gettingStarted: Open the Edit tab (route /studio/edit).
Click a tool card, for example Image Upscale.
Upload your file in the box marked with *, or paste its URL and click Add.
Pick a model in the Model dropdown if one is shown, and fill in the Prompt if one is shown.
Click Generate, wait for the result, then click Download.
tips: Start from the card whose name matches your goal: the tool already limits the Model list to models that fit it.
Use Use as input to chain steps, for example generate with AI Image Generator, then open Image Upscale and add the result with Saved or Use as input.
Bookmark /studio/edit/<tool-name> to jump straight into a tool; the browser Back button returns to the gallery.
Check the short description under the Model dropdown: it describes the selected model.
Uploads are checked by file type: an image box rejects non-image files with a message.
bestPractices: Read which boxes are marked * before you click Generate; a missing required file or Prompt shows a message and nothing runs.
Wait for "Uploading…" to finish before clicking Generate; the button is disabled while an upload is running.
Keep one tool open per task and use the This session strip to compare variations instead of re-uploading.
Use clear, direct prompts that match the placeholder shown in the Prompt box.

faqs.question: How many tools are in Edit Studio?
faqs.answer: The gallery lists 14 tool cards (counted from EDIT_TOOLS in the source).

faqs.question: Where do I open it?
faqs.answer: Click the Edit tab, or go to /studio/edit. Each tool also has its own address, /studio/edit/<tool-name>.

faqs.question: Can I filter the gallery?
faqs.answer: Yes. Click All, Image, Video or Audio above the cards.

faqs.question: Why do the upload boxes change?
faqs.answer: The boxes are built from the selected model. Change the model in the Model dropdown and the boxes and Settings update.

faqs.question: What does the * mean?
faqs.answer: A box or Prompt marked with * is required. (optional) means you can skip it.

faqs.question: Can I paste a link instead of uploading?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paste a full http:// or https:// link into the box under the upload area and click Add.

faqs.question: What does Use as input do?
faqs.answer: It adds the result to the first upload box of the matching type so you can run another pass; it confirms with 'Added as input.'

faqs.question: How do I keep my results?
faqs.answer: Click Download under each result. The This session strip is only for the current visit.

faqs.question: How do I go back to the gallery?
faqs.answer: Click ← All tools (or the browser Back button).

faqs.question: Do I need an API key?
faqs.answer: Yes, your own MuAPI key. If generation is blocked, open the API keys settings and check your MuAPI key.

studios.name: Motion Control
studios.description: Upload a reference video and one or more character images, and the studio rebuilds the video with your characters while keeping the original motion (Motion Transfer), or swaps outfits, characters or products in the same scene (Objects Swap).

studios.shortDescription: Upload a reference video and one or more character images, and the studio rebuilds the video with your characters while keeping the original motion (Motion Transfer), or swaps outfits, characters or products in the same scene (Objects Swap).
studios.fullDescription: Motion Control uses Seedance Motion Control models. You supply a reference video that holds the movement, choreography and camera work you want, plus one or more character or performer images. In Motion Transfer mode the studio extracts the motion from the video and rebuilds the scene with your characters. In Objects Swap mode the video scene is kept unchanged while outfits, characters or products are swapped for those in your images. An optional text box adds extra scene, lighting or motion notes. You choose the model, aspect ratio, duration, audio and advanced options in the bottom bar and click Generate Motion. Finished videos are shown in a gallery that is kept in your browser.

studios.modelExplanations: Pick a model from the Model menu. The menu shows each model name with the start of its description. The default is Seedance 2.5 Motion Control. Seedance 2.0 Motion Control has a lower limit of 15 seconds and 9 images and offers a High or Basic Quality choice; the 2.5 models allow up to 30 seconds and 30 images and offer a High Bitrate switch. Other 2.5 variants listed in the menu follow the same limits; read their descriptions in the menu for what makes them different.
howToSteps: Open Motion Control: choose Motion Control in the studio list, or go to /studio/motion-control.
At the top of the bottom bar choose Motion Transfer (rebuild the scene with your character using the video motion) or Objects Swap (keep the scene and swap outfits, characters or products).

Add the reference video: click the video button at the left (tooltip Upload reference video (MP4/WebM/MOV) or drag and drop) and pick a file up to 100 MB, or drag a video onto it, or click Library or Saved and choose a video. A preview shows when it is ready.

Add at least one character image: click the image button (tooltip Upload character or performer images (PNG/JPEG/WebP)) and choose one or more images up to 20 MB each, or pick images from Library (Add as Image) or Saved. Click the + button to add more; click the x on a thumbnail (tooltip Remove image) to remove one.
Optional: type extra scene, lighting or motion notes in the text box (the placeholder starts with Optional — describe additional scene details).
Optional: click the model button (Seedance 2.5 by default) and choose a model from the Model menu. Remember the 2.0 model allows at most 9 images and 15 seconds.

Click the aspect ratio button (16:9 by default) and choose from the Aspect Ratio menu. Click the duration button (5s by default) and drag the slider (starts at 4 seconds) or click a preset such as 10s.
Optional: click Generate Audio to turn sound generation on. Click the sliders icon to set High Bitrate, Quality or Seed.
Click Generate Motion. The button shows Generating... while the video is made.

When it finishes, a new card appears in the gallery. Hover over it to preview, click it to watch fullscreen, and use the download button (tooltip Download) to save it. Use Use as Video on the card to make it the next reference video.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Motion Transfer and Objects Swap?
faqs.answer: Motion Transfer rebuilds the scene with your character using the motion of the video. Objects Swap keeps the video scene unchanged and swaps outfits, characters or products.

faqs.answer: A reference video and at least one character image. Without them you get messages asking you to add them.

faqs.question: What are the file size limits?

faqs.question: How many images and how many seconds can I use?
faqs.answer: It depends on the model: Seedance 2.0 Motion Control allows up to 9 images and 15 seconds; the 2.5 models allow up to 30 images and 30 seconds. The shortest duration is 4 seconds.

faqs.question: Is the text box required?

faqs.question: What does the seed do?
faqs.answer: The Seed box in the sliders popover is -1 (random) by default. Enter a number to use a fixed seed.

faqs.question: What is the Library button for?
faqs.answer: It opens an Asset Library with Videos, Images and Results you used or created in this studio. Saved opens your shared library across studios.

faqs.question: How do I use a result as the next reference video?
faqs.answer: Click Use as Video on the result card.

faqs.question: Where is my gallery stored?
faqs.answer: In this browser only. Download the videos you want to keep.

studios.name: Zack D Studio
studios.description: A step-by-step builder for a vertical (9:16) animated explainer short: start from a topic, edit a starter script, generate character sheets and keyframe images, animate them into clips, add narration and optional music, then render the final video in your browser.
keyFeatures: Six-step guided flow with numbered step buttons: Topic, Script, Characters & keyframes, Motion clips, Voice & music, Final cut
Starter script from your topic that you edit by hand (narration and scene text for each beat and shot)
Templates: one finished demo and two script-only templates that need no paid generation to load
Three looks: Plasticine clay, Translucent glass, Bright toy studio
Character sheets and 9:16 keyframes generated as images; keyframes animated into clips
Narration with a choice of preset voices, and optional background music
Final cut rendered in your browser, with the option to keep the clips' own sound
Downloads: video, free .srt captions file; paid burned-in animated captions; post to social
Confirmation prompt before paid steps and a Redo button to retry any item
studios.howToUse: Open Zack D Studio at /studio/zackd. Type a topic and click Write starter script (or load a template), edit the script and click Approve script, then work through the steps: generate character sheets and keyframes, approve keyframes, generate clips, generate narration, and render the video in Final cut.
studios.modelCapabilities: The studio uses MuAPI models behind the scenes: nano-banana-2 for images (with flux-dev-image as a fallback), Veo 3.1 fast image-to-video for clips (with the standard Veo 3.1 image-to-video as a fallback), a MiniMax speech model for narration, Suno for music and an AI captions service for burned-in captions. There is no model selector; the only choices on screen are the look, the voice and the caption language and theme.
limitations: The starter script is a fixed skeleton
Beats and shots cannot be added or removed in the screen
Paid steps use your MuAPI credits
The rendered video is not saved across page loads
Voice cloning is not supported
The final video is 9:16 only
troubleshooting: Images, clips or audio fail
Render video fails or says the browser cannot encode video
Project is not what I expected after loading a template

studios.shortDescription: A step-by-step builder for a vertical (9:16) animated explainer short: start from a topic, edit a starter script, generate character sheets and keyframe images, animate them into clips, add narration and optional music, then render the final video in your browser.
studios.fullDescription: Zack D Studio guides you through six numbered steps: Topic, Script, Characters & keyframes, Motion clips, Voice & music and Final cut. You start with one topic (or a template). The studio writes a fixed starter script of three beats that you edit by hand. After you approve the script, you pick a look, generate character sheets and one keyframe image per shot, animate each keyframe into a clip, generate narration (and optionally music), and finally render a 720x1280 video in your browser with transitions between shots. You can download the video or an .srt caption file, post it to social media, or pay to burn animated captions into it. Every paid generation asks for confirmation first, and your project is saved in this browser. The studio is adapted from the open-source Zack D Films project.
whenToUse: You want a complete vertical animated short built step by step from a topic
You want to review and approve each stage before paying for the next
whenToUseAnother: Use Storyboard Studio to plan scenes more freely
Use Video Studio for single generated clips
Use Vibe Motion for animated graphics
studios.bestFor: Creators building short-form animated explainers who want control at each stage.

studios.modelExplanations: You do not choose models. If the first image or clip model fails or returns a placeholder, the studio tries the fallback automatically. The clips step text states that clips are animated with Veo 3.1 (fast, with the standard model as fallback), take a few minutes each and are the most expensive step. Narration uses preset MiniMax voices at a fixed speed. Music is optional.
howToSteps: Open Zack D Studio: choose Zack D Studio in the studio list, or go to /studio/zackd. Six step buttons (1. Topic to 6. Final cut) show where you are.

On the Topic step, type a question or idea in the TOPIC field (up to 200 characters), or click one of the example topic cards to fill it in. To start from a template instead, scroll to Templates and click Use as template (finished demo) or Use script.

Click Write starter script (it reads Rewrite starter script if a script already exists, and Continue current project takes you back to it). This builds a fixed three-beat script from your topic. No paid generation happens yet.
On the Script step, read the beats and edit the narration box of each beat and the scene box of each shot to fit your idea. When it reads right, click Approve script.
On the Characters & keyframes step, pick a look: Plasticine clay, Translucent glass or Bright toy studio.

In Character sheets, click Generate all character sheet(s) and confirm the prompt, or use Generate on each card. Then in Keyframes click Generate all keyframe(s) and confirm. These are paid image calls on your MuAPI key. If a card looks wrong, click Redo on it.
When every keyframe is done, click Approve keyframes to go to Motion clips.

On Motion clips click Generate all clip(s) and confirm the prompt (the most expensive step; each clip takes a few minutes). Use Redo on any single clip you do not like. When all clips exist, click Continue to audio.

On Voice & music choose a voice in the Voice dropdown, then click Generate narration (Regenerate narration if you already have one) and confirm. Optionally click Generate music under Background music (optional). Click Continue to final cut.

On Final cut leave Keep the clips' own sound (Veo audio), quieter under narration on or off as you prefer, then click Render video. Wait while it shows Rendering and a percentage; click Cancel to stop.

When the video appears, click Download video to save it. Optionally click Captions (.srt) for a free caption file, Post to social to publish it, or use Burn captions into the video (pick a Caption language and theme, then click Burn captions; the button reads Burn again once a captioned copy exists) for paid animated captions.
To start over click New project and confirm. Your current project is saved in this browser until you do.

faqs.question: Where do I open Zack D Studio?
faqs.answer: Choose Zack D Studio in the studio list, or go to /studio/zackd.

faqs.question: Does it write the script for me?
faqs.answer: It builds a fixed three-beat starter script from your topic. It is a skeleton, so edit the narration and scene text on the Script step before you approve it.

faqs.question: What costs credits?
faqs.answer: Character sheets, keyframes, clips, narration, music and burned-in captions are paid calls on your MuAPI key. Loading a template and the free .srt file cost nothing. The studio asks you to confirm before each paid batch.

faqs.question: How long does the final video render take?
faqs.answer: It renders in your browser and can take a minute or two. You can click Cancel to stop.

faqs.question: What shape is the video?
faqs.answer: Vertical 9:16, rendered at 720x1280.

faqs.question: Can I keep the sound from the generated clips?
faqs.answer: Yes. Keep the clips' own sound (Veo audio), quieter under narration is on by default in Final cut.

faqs.question: Can I clone my voice?
faqs.answer: No. Only preset voices are offered.

faqs.question: How much do burned-in captions cost?
faqs.answer: The studio says about $0.20 minimum ($0.005 per second) and 2-3 minutes. They need narration. The .srt file is free.

faqs.question: Is my work saved?
faqs.answer: The project (script, images, clips, narration, music) is saved in this browser. The rendered video is not; download it after rendering.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Use as template and Use script?
faqs.answer: Use as template loads the finished demo with its keyframes and clips. Use script loads just a script, and you generate the media yourself.

studios.businessValue: Zack D Studio puts script, images, clips, voice and final render in one guided flow, with confirmation before each paid step.
studios.competitivePositioning: Zack D Studio is a fixed, vertical-only pipeline for one short format. It is not a free-form editor; use other studios or an editor for custom layouts.
gettingStarted: Open Zack D Studio from the studio list (/studio/zackd).
To try it with no paid generation, click Use as template on Swallow gum: finished demo in the Templates section.
On the Script step, edit any text and click Approve script, then step through Approve keyframes and Continue to audio (a finished demo already has its keyframes and clips).
On Final cut click Render video and then Download video.
To make your own, start from a topic with Write starter script and follow the steps; every paid step asks for confirmation first.
bestPractices: Finish and approve the script before spending on images.
Check keyframes before generating clips, because clips are the most expensive step.
Generate narration before rendering if you want narration in the video.
Download the final video right after rendering: the rendered video is not kept if you leave or refresh the page, although the rest of the project is saved.

glossary.Beat: One unit of narration in the script, with one or more shots.
glossary.Shot: A single clip in the final video, with its own scene description.
glossary.Keyframe: The still 9:16 image that is animated into a clip.
glossary.Character sheet: A reference image of a recurring character or object.
glossary.Look: The visual style preset: Plasticine clay, Translucent glass or Bright toy studio.
glossary.Burned-in captions: Captions drawn into the video itself (paid), as opposed to the free .srt file.
